2) Stand in a circle with each noodle upright on the floor; on the signal, step one place to the right and catch your neighbor's noodle before it falls. In pairs, one partner holds a noodle and raises or lowers it while the other jumps over or limbos under it.
3) In noodle tag, the tagger touches a specific body part (back, top of the foot, etc.) and the person touched becomes the tagger; in noodle 'Cham-chamcham', face each other over a noodle in the center, play rock-paper-scissors, and the winner grabs the noodle to touch the loser, who runs to their own line.

Pool noodles (fun sticks), cones (stacking cups can substitute)
콩주머니(또는 작은 공), 스카프, 바구니, 원마커
Seated Classroom Basketball (Beanbag Pass and Shoot)

1) Split into two teams with a warm-up game: stand back to back, follow the body-part commands, and grab the scarf first; then both teams sit in a zigzag W and M formation facing each other on floor spot markers.
2) The attacking team passes a beanbag in order from player 1 to the last player, while the defenders reach out to block passes without lifting their bottoms off the floor.
3) When the beanbag reaches the last player safely, that player may try to shoot it into the basket.

Beanbags (or small balls), scarves, basket, spot markers

4) Measure the total score earned within the time limit (3 minutes).

Classroom Training 4: Core and Upper-Body Strength Workout

Classroom PE: How to Do Sport Stacking (Speed Stacks 3-3-3, 3-6-3 and Cycle)

1) Sport stacking is racing against the clock to stack and take down 12 cups by the rules, following 3 basic principles: go from left to right, alternate hands, and stack everything up (upstack) before taking it all down (downstack).
2) In the 3-3-3 event, stack three sets of 3 cups in turn, then nest them back down in order from the start.
3) In the 3-6-3 event, stack 3 cups on each side and 6 in the middle, then take them down in order.
4) The Cycle event starts from 3-6-3, goes through 6-6 and the 1-10-1 pyramid, and finishes by returning to the 3-6-3 shape.

Throwball Part 1: Scoring by Sending the Ball into Empty Space over the Net

1) Form teams of 4 and start on a volleyball or badminton court with a net; throw the ball over from the serve line into the opposing court.

Killer and Healer: Two-Team Survival Tag

Soccer-Style Game: Dribble the Balls Home

1) Draw start lines for the two groups 15m apart and place balls (one per group member) on dish cones behind each line.
2) At the start, run to the other group's side and dribble a ball from their cone back to your own side with your feet; you may not kick it hard and run after it, but must dribble it accurately.
3) Place the ball on your own group's dish cone and run back to the other group; balls being dribbled cannot be stolen from each other.

Soccer-Style Game: Dribble and Pass to a Teammate

1) Set cones at both ends with spot markers 3m apart between them, and form groups of 4.
2) Player 1 dribbles around the front cone and on to the far cone, makes a long pass to Player 4 and moves to Player 4's spot; Player 4 passes short to Player 3 and takes Player 3's spot, and Player 3 passes short to Player 2 and takes Player 2's spot.

4 tall cones (2 start/finish, 2 turnaround), whistle, stopwatch/smartphone

Rolling Foam-Dice-Ball Individual Tag — Number Roll & Fitness Task Tag

Foam dodgeball, turnaround cones, team pinnies, timer

Cooperative Circle Hoop Pass — 1-Hoop Race & 2-Hoop Opposite Vertical Cross

1) Group members hold hands in a circle and pass hula hoops around the circle by stepping and ducking through without ever unclasping hands.

Hula-Hoop Train Relay — 4-Hoop Touching Chain Advance

1) Mark start and finish lines with cones; each 4-player team places 4 hula hoops in a tight line and stands 1 player per hoop.

Hula hoops (1 per student, 4 per team), 4 tall cones

Build & Knock Down the Hula-Hoop Cube — 2-Pair Construction & Target Throw Relay

Hula hoops (6 per team), foam balls (1–2 per team), cones

Hula-Hoop Train 2.0 (Treasure Collector) — Cooperative Hoop-Chain Beanbag Hunt

Hula hoops (4 per team), 4-color beanbags, 4 boundary cones

Ant Tagger — Block the Open Spot! Whole-Class Cooperative Spot Defense

1) Scatter spot markers across the floor equal to the total number of participants; everyone except 1 Ant Tagger stands on a spot, leaving exactly 1 open spot marker (the anthole).

Spot markers (equal to total players including tagger), 1-minute timer

Pinwheel Running Game — 3-Spoke Radial Spot Sprint with Left/Right Calls

2) The tagger walks or jogs around the outside perimeter in either direction.

Ball-Baton Cooperative Pursuit Relay — 3-Team Track Chase & Over-Under Pass

1) Mark a circular track with spot markers and place 3 teams in single-file lines spaced 120 degrees apart at 3 cones, with each front runner holding a ball.

Survival Cooperative Endurance Pursuit — 1-Lap Baton-Pass Team Elimination Run

1) Divide the class into two teams starting 180 degrees apart on a small oval track (marked by cones), with 1 runner per team holding a soft foam hammer/stick.

Four Square — 4-Quadrant One-Bounce Hand Strike & King-of-the-Court Rotation

1) Divide a 4m×4m square into four 2m×2m squares numbered 1 (highest) to 4 (lowest); in groups of 5–6, 4 players occupy squares 1–4 while players 5–6 wait in line.
2) Player 1 serves by bouncing the ball once and hitting it diagonally into Square 3; from then on, each player must let the ball bounce once in their square before hitting it with one or two hands into any other square.
3) A player is out if they hit the ball before it bounces, let it bounce twice, hit a line or out-of-bounds, touch the ball with non-hand body parts, or catch and throw the ball.
4) The eliminated player goes to the waiting line, lower-ranked players rotate up one square (waiter enters Square 4), and the 3 remaining players on court each earn 1 point toward a 15-point win.
1 bouncy ball (Four Square ball or volleyball), floor tape or court line markers
폭신주사위공 찜피구 — 앉아서 패스 이동 & 팔 뻗어 터치하는 교실 무투척 피구
Seated Foam-Dice-Ball Tag Dodgeball — Pass-and-Reach Classroom Tag Game

1) Divide the class into two teams wearing pinnies and give each team 1 foam dice ball (teams may only handle their own team’s ball).
2) All players remain seated on the floor; players without the ball may scoot around freely while seated, whereas the player holding the ball cannot move from their spot.
3) Teammates pass their ball to players positioned near opponents, and the ball holder stretches out their arm while seated to tag an opponent directly with the ball.
4) Tagged players step outside the boundary, perform 5 frog jumps, and immediately re-enter; the team with more active players when time expires wins.
2 foam dice balls (or soft foam balls), team pinnies
교실트레이닝 10종 전신운동 루틴 — 런지·버피·슈퍼맨·스케이트 점프 건강체력 기르기
Classroom Full-Body Fitness 10-Exercise Routine — Lunges, Burpees, Superman & Skater Jumps

1) Stand in personal space in the classroom or gym and follow a 10-exercise full-body conditioning sequence.
2) Lower-Body & Cardio (1–5): perform right-leg reverse lunges, left-leg reverse lunges, jumping jacks, standing inchworm walkouts to plank and back, and high-jump burpees.
3) Core & Balance (6–8): lie down for alternating cross-body starfish toe touches, hold a 15-second kneeling Superman balance on each diagonal, and hop side-to-side with arm swings in skater jumps.
4) Core Sit-to-Stand & Martial Kick (9–10): lie flat and stand up without using hands to engage the abs, then finish with alternating 1-2 punches into a front kick.
동그라미 고무줄 달리기 — 8자 궤적 원 작게·크게 변화시키기 협력 이어달리기
Circle Elastic-Band Relay — Figure-8 Shrink-and-Expand Human Circle Relay

1) Place 2 cones 10m apart; two teams form a circle around their respective cone in clockwise order from Player 1 to the last player, with Player 1 holding a team pinny as a baton.
2) On the whistle, Player 1 runs in a figure-8 pattern—looping clockwise around their own team’s circle and counterclockwise around the opposing team’s circle—before handing the pinny to Player 2.
3) Waiting teammates actively huddle tight around their cone to shrink the circle when their own runner loops around, then step back to expand into a giant circle when the opposing runner loops around them.
4) Continue through the final runner; the first team whose anchor hands the pinny back to Player 1 and sits down together wins.
2 tall cones, 2 team pinnies (used as batons)
한마음 달리기 (단체추발 이어달리기) — 후미 주자 배턴콘 전진 배치 & 모둠 추격전
라바콘(모둠 수×2개, 모둠별 다른 색깔 권장), 팀조끼
One-Heart Team Pursuit Relay — Rear-Runner Cone Placement & Group Overtake

1) Mark a circular track (12-pace radius) with station cones spaced equally (90° for 4 teams, 60° for 6 teams) and place a team-colored baton cone beside each start station.
2) Form 4-player teams in single file (1–2–3–4) wearing matching pinnies, with Rear Runner #4 holding the baton cone.
3) On the whistle, the whole group runs together; before reaching the next station cone, Runner #4 must sprint to the front of their group and set the baton cone down at that station while front teammates pace down to let them pass.
4) As the line passes the station, the new last runner (#3) picks up the baton cone, sprints to the front, and sets it at the next station; overtaking and tagging the group ahead scores 2 points (caught group 0 pts, other groups 1 pt).
Tall cones (2 per team in distinct colors), team pinnies
공을 던지고 받으며 득점하는 게임 — 원마커 위 캐치 성공 시 원마커 수거 릴레이
Throw-and-Catch Spot Collector — Catch on the Spot Marker to Score

1) Mark a start line and scatter plenty of spot markers across the court beyond the line; form teams of 4 and set a rotation order (1–4).
2) On the signal, Player 1 runs out and stands on any spot marker while Player 2 throws the ball from the start line to Player 1.
3) If Player 1 catches the ball cleanly while standing on the spot marker, they pick up the spot marker and run both the spot and the ball back to the start line.
4) Player 1 hands the ball to Player 3 while Player 2 runs out to a new spot marker to catch Player 3’s throw (if a catch is dropped, leave the spot marker and bring back only the ball); the team with the most spot markers when time expires wins.
Balls (1 per team), spot markers, team pinnies
공 연결 기차 놀이 — 사각형 원마커 패스 앤 런(Give & Go) 빈 공간 이동 릴레이
농구공(또는 소프트볼, 모둠당 1개), 원마커(한 변에 5개씩 사각형 배치), 팀조끼, 초시계
Ball-Connection Train Relay — Square-Court Pass & Cut to the Open Spot

1) Arrange spot markers 3m apart with 5 spots per side to form a square court; place a 5-player team in order along the spots.
2) On the whistle, the ball holder passes the ball along the side of the square to the teammate standing on the spot ahead.
3) Immediately after passing, the passer sprints across the inside of the court to occupy the next open spot marker ahead of the line.
4) Continue passing along the perimeter while sprinting to the next open spot; time how fast the team completes 3 full laps around the square, or run two teams simultaneously on opposite sides of the same square for a pursuit race.
Basketballs or soft balls (1 per team), spot markers (5 per side of square), team pinnies, stopwatch
양말공 표적도전 (스트라이크 삼진 아웃) — 종이컵 10개 타깃 오버핸드 투수 이닝 게임
Sock-Ball Target Pitching (Strike Three Out!) — 10-Cup Strike Zone Inning Challenge

1) Line up 10 paper cups along the front edge of a desk or table and place 2 remaining cups on the floor 10 paces away to mark the pitching rubber.
2) Hold 3 rolled sock balls and throw overhand like a baseball pitcher—raising the ball above the head and snapping through the shoulder, elbow, and wrist toward the cup target.
3) Hitting and knocking off at least 1 cup counts as a Strike; missing all cups counts as a Ball (3 strikes = 1 strikeout; 4 balls = 1 walk).
4) Pitch until you record 3 outs (1 full inning) while tracking total batters faced and walks allowed, aiming to finish the inning in the fewest batters possible.
3 rolled sock balls (or beanbags), 12 paper/stacking cups, desk or table
순환 태그 게임 — 2인 추격자 릴레이 교대 & 무탈락 도망자 팀 대항 태그전
구역 표시용 콘, 출발점 원마커, 점수판, 팀조끼
Rotational Tag Game — 2-Chaser Relay Tag & Zero-Elimination Team Battle

1) Cones mark a rectangular court with a spot marker and scoreboard at the chasers’ start line; one team enters the court as Runners while the Chaser team lines up in numbered order at the start spot.
2) On the whistle, Chasers #1 and #2 enter the court together to pursue and tag any Runner.
3) As soon as a Chaser tags 1 Runner, that Chaser sprints back to the start spot, high-fives the next waiting teammate to tag them in, and flips the team scoreboard up by 1 point.
4) Tagged Runners are never eliminated and keep dodging continuously; swap team roles after a set time and compare total tag points to declare the winner.
Boundary cones, start spot marker, flip scoreboard, team pinnies
티볼형 게임 (공 치고, 달리고, 공 이어 주기) — 6인 순환 타격·중계송구 복합 움직임 게임
배팅티, 티볼 배트, 티볼공(안전 공), 반환점 라바콘
Tee-Ball Hit, Run & Relay Game — 6-Player Role-Rotation Batting & Relay Throw

1) Place a batting tee and 1 turnaround cone 10m ahead; form groups of 6 and assign rotational roles (#1 batter, #2–5 fielders, #6 catcher).
2) The batter hits the ball off the tee and sprints around the 10m cone and back while fielders field the ball and relay-throw it through middle cut-off teammates to the catcher.
3) Play stops when the catcher places the ball back on the batting tee, and everyone rotates roles after every single at-bat (catcher becomes batter, batter joins fielders).
4) Progression: require all 4 fielders to touch the ball before the catcher places it on the tee, while the batter continuously shuttles around the 10m cone to score 1 point per lap.
Batting tee, tee-ball bat, soft tee-ball, turnaround cone
콘 아이스크림 놀이 4단계 — 콘 위 공 균형 이동·플레이스틱 술래잡기·밸런스 패치 릴레이
라바콘(인원수만큼), 크기별 공(폼볼·배구공·탱탱볼 등), 플레이스틱(펀스틱), 반환점 콘
4-Stage Ice Cream Cone Progression — Balance Walk, Noodle Tag & Handicap Relay

1) Stage 1 (Adaptation): Hold an inverted cone topped with a ball like an ice cream cone and progress from walking to speed-walking, running, and tossing-and-catching.
2) Stage 2 (Individual Tag): Protect your own ball while knocking others' balls off their cones; anyone whose ball drops performs 3 jumping jacks where they retrieve it to revive.
3) Stage 3 (Foam-Stick Tag): Hold the ice cream cone in one hand and a foam stick in the other to extend attacking reach and increase activity volume.
4) Stage 4 (Ice Cream Cone Relay): Sprint around the turning cone and loop once around your team line before passing the cone-and-ball baton; if the ball drops, return to the start line and re-run.
Cones (1 per student), assorted-size balls, foam sticks, turning cones
공 맞혀 콘 뺏기 게임 — 4대2 드리블·패스 돌파 및 2m 슈팅 콘 획득 축구형 게임
축구공 또는 폼볼(모둠당 2개), 라바콘 12개(진영별 6개), 팀조끼(수비 표시용)
Kick-and-Claim Cone Raid — 4v2 Dribble-Pass Breakthrough & 2m Target Shoot Game

1) Mark shooting lines at both ends of a rectangular court and set 6 cones spaced evenly 2m behind each line.
2) Divide into two 6-player teams (4 attackers and 2 defenders wearing pinnies tied around their hands) with 2 balls per team.
3) Attackers dribble or pass to the opponent's shooting line, place the ball stationary, and kick to hit a cone; a hit lets them bring that cone back to their side, while a miss sends them back to the start line.
4) Defenders intercept and kick attackers' balls out of bounds (forcing a restart from the start line); the team holding more cones when time expires wins.
4 Soccer/foam balls (2 per team), 12 cones (6 per end), pinnies
앉아 협동 풍선 튀기기 — 의자 착석 손잡고 손·머리 풍선 랠리 교실 협동 놀이
풍선(모둠당 1개, 여유분 포함), 교실 책상 및 의자, 초시계
Seated Cooperative Balloon Keep-Up — Linked-Hands & Head-Save Classroom Rally

1) Arrange desks in group clusters and have teammates sit on their chairs while holding hands in a closed circle.
2) Toss a balloon into the air and keep it up using linked hands and heads.
3) Both hands and heads are legal, but only linked-hand hits count toward the score (headers only save the rally).
4) A group is eliminated immediately if anyone's hips leave their chair, if hands unlink during a hit, or if the balloon touches the floor; run two timed practice-and-measurement rounds.
Balloons (1 per group plus spares), classroom desks and chairs, timer
공으로 풍선 오래 살리기 — 공 패스 앤 히트 1분 릴레이 교실 협응성 놀이
풍선(모둠당 1개), 작고 가벼운 공(폼볼 등 모둠당 1개), 초시계
Ball-Hit Balloon Keep-Up — Pass-the-Ball & Strike 1-Minute Coordination Challenge

1) Form groups of 3-4 students and give each group 1 balloon and 1 small ball.
2) One teammate tosses the balloon up while the ball holder strikes the balloon upward using the ball in their hands.
3) After striking the balloon once, the player must immediately pass the ball to a teammate, who then strikes the balloon next.
4) The attempt ends if the balloon hits the floor, if the same player hits it twice in a row, or if the balloon touches any body part; sum the best counts from two 1-minute trials.
1 Balloon and 1 small soft ball per group of 3-4, timer
다함께 풍선 오래 살리기 — 원형 손잡고 온몸 타격 & 큰 풍선·작은 풍선 단계별 협동 놀이
큰 풍선 및 작은 풍선(모둠당 각 1~2개)
All-Together Circle Balloon Keep-Up — Full-Body Linked-Hand Rally (Large to Small Balloon)

1) Group members form a circle and hold hands firmly.
2) Toss a balloon into the air and move together as a linked ring to keep the balloon from touching the floor.
3) Players may use their linked hands, heads, shoulders, knees, or feet—any body part—as long as the hand chain stays unbroken.
4) Start Stage 1 with a large, slow-floating balloon, then advance in Stage 2 to a small, fast-dropping balloon; the group that keeps it airborne longest wins.
Large and small balloons (1-2 each per group)
스포츠스태킹 3-6-3 릴레이 — 2.13m 출발선 교대 규칙 및 패자부활 토너먼트
스피드스택스 컵 세트(모둠당 1세트), 스택매트 및 타이머(선택), 책상, 라인 테이프
Sport Stacking 3-6-3 Team Relay — Official 2.13m Start-Line Changeover & Consolation Bracket

1) Set up two tables with Speed Stacks sets and mark the official start line with tape 2.13m away from the tables.
2) Form 4-player teams numbered 1 to 4; Runner 1 starts at the table while Runners 2-4 wait behind the 2.13m start line.
3) On signal, Runner 1 up-stacks and down-stacks the 3-6-3 pattern, turns, and sprints across the start line to release Runner 2; after Runner 4 finishes, stop the timer or place hands on head.
4) If the next runner leaves before the returning runner's foot touches or crosses the start line, they must run back to touch the line before stacking.
Speed Stacks cup sets, stack mats and timers (optional), tables, floor tape
협동 Up & Down 공 이어달리기 — 머리 위·다리 사이 교차 패스 및 1.5바퀴 콘 순환 릴레이
Cooperative Up & Down Ball Relay — Over-Under Line Pass & 1.5-Lap Cone Sprint

1) Each group stands in a single-file line between a front cone and a back cone, with the front player holding a ball.
2) On signal, the first player passes the ball overhead to the second player, who passes it under between their legs to the third, alternating Up and Down all the way to the last player.
3) The last player takes the ball, sprints forward around the front cone, runs all the way back around the rear cone, and finishes at the front of the line (1.5 laps total).
4) Meanwhile, teammates step back one spot to open the front position and repeat the Up & Down pass until everyone completes a run.
1 Volleyball or foam ball per group, 2 cones per group (front and back)
풍차 이어달리기 — 원형 트랙 다모둠 추격 릴레이 및 호루라기 방향 전환 변형 게임
릴레이 배턴(또는 펀스틱, 모둠당 1개), 트랙 표시용 접시콘, 호루라기
Pinwheel Pursuit Relay — Multi-Team Circular Track Chase & Double-Whistle Direction Reversal

1) Mark a large circular track with disc cones and station 3-6 teams at equal intervals inside the circle (numbered 1-4), with only Runner 1 holding a baton on the outer track.
2) On a single whistle, all #1 runners sprint one lap in the same direction and pass the baton to #2; teams continue cycling through runners until one team catches and tags the runner ahead of them.
3) Award 2 points to the tagging team, 0 points to the tagged team, and 1 point to all other teams.
4) Variation: whenever the teacher blows a double whistle (Peep-peep!), all runners immediately reverse direction around the circle, turning the hunted into the hunter.
Relay batons (1 per team), disc cones for circular track, whistle
꼬리잡기 3종 — 원조 개인전·운동 미션 무한 부활·모둠별 꼬리 나눔 협력 꼬리잡기
3-Stage Tail Tag Progression — Classic Spare-Tail, Exercise Revival & Team Tail-Sharing Tag

1) Stage 1 (Classic Tail Tag): Tuck a pinnie into the back of your waistband as a tail; carry captured tails in your hand as extra lives to re-tuck if yours is pulled (3-minute rounds).
2) Stage 2 (Revival Tail Tag): Players who lose all tails run to the teacher, complete 10 frog jumps, jumping jacks, or squats, and receive a fresh tail to re-enter immediately.
3) Stage 3 (Team Cooperative Tail Tag): Form 3-4 player squads wearing matching team pinnies plus waist tails.
4) Teammates share captured spare tails with eliminated squadmates so they can revive immediately; the team holding the most tails at time-up wins.
Team pinnies (2x the number of students)
공 차고 콘 돌아오기 게임 — 7m(1점)·12m(2점) 거리 선택 주루 및 수비용 홈 송구 발야구
배구공 또는 소프트 축구공 1개, 베이스 2개(공격용·수비용 홈), 티대용 접시콘 1개, 반환점 라바콘 2개, 팀조끼
Kick & Round the Cone — 7m (1-Pt) vs 12m (2-Pt) Risk-Reward Kickball Lead-Up

1) Place an offensive home base and a defensive home base side by side with a disc-cone tee between them, and set a near cone at 7m (1 point) and a far cone at 12m (2 points).
2) The kicker kicks the stationary ball off the disc cone and chooses whether to round the 7m cone for 1 point or the 12m cone for 2 points before returning to offensive home.
3) Fielders retrieve the ball and relay-pass it back to defensive home; if the ball reaches defensive home before the runner steps on offensive home, the runner is out.
4) Swap offense and defense after every player kicks once, and play 2 innings.
1 Volleyball/soccer ball, 2 home bases, 1 disc cone (tee), 2 turning cones (7m & 12m), pinnies
모든 수비수에게 공 이어주기 게임 — 3인 동반 주루 대 전원 원마커 착석 패스 발야구
배구공 1개, 베이스 4개, 수비 위치용 원마커, 점수판, 팀조끼
Pass-to-Every-Defender Kickball — 3-Runner Squad Sprint vs All-Fielders Poly-Spot Sit-Down Relay

1) Set up a 4-base diamond and scatter poly spots across the field for every defender.
2) Divide the batting team into 3-player squads; when the pitcher rolls the ball and the kicker kicks, all 3 squadmates run the bases together.
3) The first fielder to field the ball steps on their poly spot, passes to the next fielder, and sits down; every defender must receive the ball on their spot and sit down.
4) Scoring is based on the LAST runner of the 3-player squad when the final defender sits: reaching home scores 1 point, plus 1 extra point for each additional base reached.
1 Volleyball, 4 bases, poly spots (1 per defender), scoreboard, pinnies
공을 차고 뛰며 공을 던지는 전략형 게임 — 20m 안전지대 체류·귀환 및 마지막 타자 5점 제한 발야구
소프트 배구공/축구공 1개, 홈 베이스 1개, 투수용 원마커 1개, 안전지대 및 파울라인용 라바콘, 팀조끼
Strategic Kick-Run-Throw Kickball — 20m Safe-Zone Hold & Last-Batter 5-Point Cap

1) Place home plate at the kicking box, a pitcher's poly spot 7m ahead, and a safe-zone gate marked by 2 cones 20m ahead.
2) The pitcher rolls the ball and the kicker kicks and sprints to the 20m safe zone; fielders retire runners by catching fly balls or throwing/tagging below the shoulders while runners are between zones.
3) Runners may wait in the safe zone and sprint back to home plate on subsequent kicks to score 1 point each.
4) On the final kicker's turn, all waiting runners must sprint home (capped at a maximum of 5 points; a caught fly ball nullifies all runs) while the final kicker runs to the safe zone and straight back home for 1 point.
1 Soft volleyball/soccer ball, 1 home base, 1 pitcher poly spot (7m), safe-zone cones (20m), pinnies
달리기가 빠를까? 공이 빠를까? — 외곽 14m 주루 대 내측 10m 4베이스 송구 레이스 발야구
배구공 1개, 베이스 8개(공격용 4개·수비용 4개), 티대용 접시콘 1개, 점수판, 팀조끼
Who Is Faster: Runner or Ball? — 14m Outer Base-Run vs 10m Inner 4-Base Relay Throw Kickball

1) Set up a double diamond: an outer running diamond (14m between bases) and an inner fielding diamond (10m between bases), with a volleyball on a disc-cone tee at offensive home.
2) Playing 6v6, the kicker kicks the stationary ball off the cone and sprints around all four outer 14m bases (1st, 2nd, 3rd, and Home) nonstop.
3) Fielders retrieve the ball, throw it to the nearest inner 10m base, and relay-pass the ball around all four inner bases in order.
4) If the runner crosses outer home first, offense scores 1 point; if the ball completes the 4 inner bases first, the runner is out (3 innings).
1 Volleyball, 8 bases (4 outer at 14m, 4 inner at 10m), 1 disc-cone tee, scoreboard, pinnies
골대 차지하기 게임 — 10m 정육각형 6골대 콘 격파 소유권 전환 축구형 게임
Claim-the-Goal Hexagon Soccer — 10m 6-Goal Cone Knockdown & Ownership Flip Game

1) Mark a regular hexagon court (10m between vertices) and set 3 cones side by side at each of the 6 vertices to form 6 goals.
2) Divide into two teams starting with 3 goals and 2 soccer balls each (4 balls total in play).
3) Kick a ball to knock down any cone of an opponent's 3-cone goal (knocking down even 1 of the 3 cones flips ownership); stand the cone back up and that goal now belongs to your team.
4) No fixed goalkeepers are assigned—any player may defend any goal without using hands—and the team owning more of the 6 goals when time expires wins.
4 Soccer balls (2 per team), 18 cones (3 per vertex at 6 vertices), pinnies
공 줄다리기 게임 — 5선 코트 중앙 2콘 게이트 동시 패스 통과 및 골문 전진 대결
축구공(모둠당 1~2개), 중앙 골문용 라바콘 2개, 라인기(또는 라인 테이프/분필)
Soccer Tug-of-War — 5-Line Court 2-Cone Gate Accuracy Kick & Goal-Push Duel

1) Draw 5 parallel lines on the ground and place 2 cones on the center (3rd) line to form a target gate.
2) Two 4-player teams line up facing each other behind the outer start lines and set their kicking order.
3) Pairs of opposing kickers take turns kicking a ground ball through the 2-cone gate (any ball kicked into the air counts as a miss).
4) If both make it or both miss, it is a tie and the cones stay put; if only one succeeds, that team moves both cones one line closer to the opponent's side, and the team that pushes the gate farther by time-up wins.
Soccer balls (1-2 per team), 2 cones for the target gate, line chalk or tape
Learning the Basic Forward Roll on a Mat

1) Stand in front of the mat, then crouch down with feet together and knees bent.
2) Tuck the chin tightly to the chest, round the body, place both hands on the mat, push off with the feet and roll forward.
3) The body should touch the mat in this order: hands, back of the head, shoulders, back, hips, feet.
4) Use the rotation momentum to land on the soles of the feet and stand up.
Learning the Basic Backward Roll on a Mat

1) Sit with your back to the mat and raise both hands beside the ears with palms facing up.
2) Tuck the chin and curl into a ball, then roll backward starting with the hips.
3) The body should touch the mat in this order: hips, back, shoulders, then head and hands.
4) At the end, push strongly against the mat with both hands, swing the legs over and stand up right away.

1) Set up cones at the start line and turnaround point to mark the movement zone.
2) Perform the basic locomotor skills in order: walking, running, and jumping with both feet.
3) Practice hopping on one foot and rhythmic skipping, which combines a step and a hop.
4) Finish with galloping (lead foot steps, back foot follows) and leaping (a long one-foot takeoff) so students learn all 7 movements in turn.

1) Lay a long mat and get into the ready position facing the direction of travel.
2) Step one foot forward, lean the upper body down, and place the first hand and then the second hand on the mat.
3) Kick the back leg up hard and rotate with the body stretched out in a straight line in the air.
4) Land on the first foot and then the second foot, and stand up fully.
신문지, 색종이(또는 A4용지), 가위, 테이프, 필기도구(매직/포스트잇)

1) Cut 5 holes in a sheet of newspaper, write scores from 10 to 50 beside each hole, and tape it to the door frame as a target board.
2) Set a start line three steps away from the target.
3) Do 1 jumping jack before each throw, then fly the paper airplane.
4) Add up the points scored by flying through the holes and time how long it takes to reach a total of 200 points or more.
Newspaper, colored paper (or A4 paper), scissors, tape, writing tools (markers/sticky notes)

1) Arrange 16 chairs in a 4x4 grid in the center of the classroom; the two teams sit at desks along opposite walls and are numbered from 1.
2) The teacher calls a random number, and the student with that number from each team runs out and tries to claim an empty chair first.
3) In the second version, students play rock-paper-scissors, then the teacher calls 'winner' or 'loser' and the called student either tags the opponent or dodges them to sit on a chair.
4) The first team to complete two bingo lines (row, column or diagonal) wins.

1) Rearrange the desks into two sides to create a snail-shaped path around the classroom, and have each team line up by group at the corners.
2) At the signal, each team's first runner moves along the aisle between desks and plays rock-paper-scissors when meeting an opposing runner.
3) The winner keeps advancing; the loser returns to the back of their own team's line and the next runner starts immediately.
4) A team wins by reaching the opposing team's starting point first or by taking the VIP seat set up with a chair.

1) Arrange chairs in a circle; with everyone's head down, the teacher secretly assigns the Mafia role.
2) Remove one chair so one 'it' player stands in the middle; everyone raises a hand and plays rock-paper-scissors with 'it'. Those who lose or tie must quickly stand up and swap to another empty chair.
3) The Mafia must always move seats regardless of the result, while the citizens observe who moves.
4) After 'it' has changed several times, citizens point out and vote with raised hands to find the Mafia; they win if they find all the Mafia within the allowed number of chances.
새학기 3종 놀이 (손님 모셔오기, 스피드 전기게임, 사랑합니다 왜요)
학생용 의자, 잡을 물건(풀 등), 배경음악
Three New-Semester Games (Bring the Guest, Speed Electric Relay, 'I Love You—Why?')

1) 'Bring the Guest': sitting in a circle, the two friends beside the empty chair hold hands and bring another friend to the empty seat, aiming to leave no empty seat when the music stops.
2) 'Speed Electric Relay': stand in a circle split into two teams and pass a hand squeeze along the line on the teacher's signal; the team that grabs the object on the opposite side first wins.
3) 'I Love You—Why?': one 'it' player says 'I love you' to a particular friend and, depending on the follow-up question, students with the named trait quickly swap seats.
4) The games are designed so that students hold hands, break the awkwardness at the start of the school year and get to know each other naturally.
Student chairs, an object to grab (e.g., glue stick), background music

1) Two or more students pair up and play the Sse-Sse-Sse hand-clapping game to the song 'Tadpole and Frog'.
2) At set points in the lyrics (e.g., 'by the stream', 'wiggle-wiggle'), they play rock-paper-scissors.
3) The winner swings both arms forward, and the loser ducks down slightly to dodge as a quick-reaction move; on a tie, both spin once on the spot.
4) Once comfortable, expand to groups of 3 or 4, or a wider formation, and enjoy it as a group reflex game.
A4용지, 필기도구, 바구니, 칠판, 보드마카, 의자

1) Name Relay: everyone writes their name on a slip of paper and cuts it into letter pieces into a basket; group members take turns in a relay, drawing pieces to rebuild a friend's name.
2) Word Combination Relay: draw letters the same way and have each group form and write as many words as possible on the board.
3) Self-Intro Round the Bases: students write OX quiz questions about themselves, and those who answer correctly advance through 1st, 2nd and 3rd base to home.
4) Self-Intro Seat Swap: sit in a circle; 'it' in the middle poses an OX question about themselves, and students whose answer differs from 'it's quickly find an empty seat and move.
A4 paper, writing tools, basket, blackboard, board markers, chairs
의자, 실내화, 작은 공, 풀(또는 작은 물건), 팀조끼, 타이머, 칠판

1) Sit in a circle and pass a clap around like dominoes, challenging the whole class to shorten its record time.
2) Bring the Guest: the two students beside an empty seat hold hands, fetch another friend and seat them, repeating for 1 minute to set a record for the most people. Foot Pass: pass an indoor shoe or ball around the circle using only the feet.
3) Speed Electric Relay: holding hands, pass a squeeze signal toward the target in the center, and the last person tries to snatch the object first.
4) Tightrope Line-Up: standing on chairs without stepping to the floor, move seats to line up in order of palm size or birthday.
Chairs, indoor shoes, small ball, glue stick (or small object), team pinnies, timer, blackboard

1) Stage 1: starting with 2 people and growing to the whole group, sit on the floor with feet together and hands clasped, then stand up at the same time.
2) Stage 2: while holding hands, balance a ball on arms and bodies and pass it around the group or the whole circle without dropping it. Stage 3, Untangle the Hands: cross hands and hold on, then, without letting go, twist and step over until the group unravels into a round circle.
3) Stage 4, Cooperative Balloon Keep-Up: holding hands without letting go, use body parts to keep the balloon in the air without touching the floor.
4) Stage 5: holding hands, pass a hula hoop from person to person using only body movement.
Small ball, balloon, hula hoop, stopwatch
Two Falling-Down Rock-Paper-Scissors Games for Staying In

1) Two players face each other and play rock-paper-scissors.
2) In 'Until You Fall', each loss lowers your posture in order: kneel on one knee, kneel on both knees, then lie down with an arm as a pillow.
3) The first to lose 4 times loses the match. In 'Butt-Drop RPS', each loss lowers you deeper into a squat, and whoever can't hold on and drops to the floor first loses.
4) Three or four or more players can also join in.

1) Push chairs under the desks and stand in front of your seat, ready to go.
2) When the teacher calls 'Island', move to the spot in front of the desk; when the teacher calls 'Sea', move to the aisle space beside the desk.
3) Anyone who moves late, goes the wrong way or flinches is out and sits down.
4) After whole-class practice, play as team competitions by row or as an individual survival game to find the last player standing.

1) At the start signal, walk freely around the classroom and play rock-paper-scissors with whoever you meet.
2) The loser places both hands on the winner's back and follows like a train car; when trains meet, the front players compete, and the whole losing train attaches behind the winning train, which grows longer.
3) If the front players tie, everyone shouts 'Bang!', all trains explode, unlink at once, and everyone starts over alone.
4) If one single line is completed without a tie, the whole train plays a final rock-paper-scissors against the homeroom teacher.
모둠별 연산 문제지 1장, 연필 1자루, 지우개 1개, 스톱워치/타이머

1) For each group, place only runner 1's desk at a distance toward the front of the board, with 1 pencil, 1 eraser and a worksheet ready.
2) When the timer and music start, student 1 focuses for 30 seconds and solves any arithmetic problems they choose.
3) After 30 seconds the teacher calls 'Switch!'; student 1 runs back to the waiting seats and hands the pencil to student 2, who hurries to the front desk and continues solving for 30 seconds, and the relay carries on in order.
4) When time is up, each group's correct answers are scored to decide the winner.
1 arithmetic worksheet per group, 1 pencil, 1 eraser, stopwatch/timer

1) With all students lying head-down on their desks, the teacher quietly selects one student as the vampire.
2) At the start signal, students walk freely around the room and shake hands with whoever they make eye contact with, waving three big times. The vampire infects a partner by firmly scratching their palm with a finger without being noticed.
3) An infected student does not collapse right away; after shaking hands with 3 more people, they cry 'Aargh!' and go to the graveyard (a designated area).
4) A citizen who spots the vampire can stand on a chair at the teacher's desk, shout 'Attention!' and accuse; if the accusation is wrong, both the accuser and the accused are out. Citizens win if they identify the vampire before half the class is infected.

1) Two players face each other with a doll or small object placed in the middle.
2) When the leader calls a body part such as head, eyes or knees, both players touch it with both hands.
3) When the leader shouts 'Jip-eo!' (Grab it!), the player who grabs the object in the middle first wins.
4) If a player touches the object when the leader says a confusing word like 'Jip-jung' or 'Jip-e ga', they are disqualified or lose.

1) Two or more players sit facing each other on the floor and hold hands.
2) Without letting go, they keep a balloon in the air using their hands, feet, head and other body parts.
3) Lifting the hips off the floor or letting go of the held hands is a foul.
4) The goal is to reach a target number of hits (e.g., 10 or 20) or to keep the balloon up without dropping it for a set time.

1) With all students lying head-down on their desks, the teacher taps one student on the back to secretly designate the Silent Mafia.
2) At the signal, students walk around freely, meet 3 friends, shake hands slowly with 3 waves each, and then sit down. The teacher secretly records on a checklist whom the Mafia shakes hands with.
3) After everyone is seated and heads are down again, the teacher calls the names of the 3 victims who shook hands with the Mafia, and they move to 'jail'.
4) Surviving students narrow down the suspect by pointing and voting; the citizens win if they catch the Mafia within 3 rounds.
소프트 폼볼, 특수 능력 카드 세트

1) Set the desks facing each other to form the court, and each student randomly receives one character card listing a unique ability.
2) The game follows basic dodgeball rules played from the seat: dodge incoming balls or throw them to hit the opposing side.
3) Hit players are out and line up beside their team, and they revive in order when a teammate catches a ball. When catching a ball or meeting a certain condition, players show their card to activate a unique superpower such as invincibility, freeze, rubber body or vampire.
4) The team that eliminates all opposing players first wins.
Soft foam balls, special-ability card set

1) The teacher writes a two-letter Korean initial-consonant pair (e.g., ㅇㅈ) on the board, and every student thinks of one word with those initials and draws it on a mini whiteboard.
2) After 3–5 minutes of drawing, students cover their boards; at the start signal they walk around without speaking, only showing their drawings, and look for friends they think drew the same word to form pairs or groups.
3) When time is up, each group comes forward and reveals its drawings and words at the same time to check whether the words match.
4) A group scores if all members match and no one elsewhere drew the same word; if even one student who drew the same word was left out of the group, the group gets 0 points.
Individual mini whiteboards, board markers, erasers

1) Push absent students' desks to the wall and widen the gaps between desks to secure aisles, then split the class into 'gimbap ingredient' groups of 4–5 students each (seaweed, rice, pickled radish, spinach, carrot, etc.).
2) Choose the first 'it' player, remove their chair, and have them stand in the middle of the room.
3) Everyone circles their hands and chants 'Roll the gimbap'; when 'it' calls 2–3 ingredients, students in those groups move to empty seats.
4) When 'it' shouts 'Roll the gimbap!', everyone must swap seats, and whoever fails to get a chair becomes the next 'it'.

1) Students push their chairs under the desks and wait at the back of the classroom or in the hallway.
2) One chosen 'it' player comes to the front of the room and, at the start signal, tags the classmates who flee at a fast walk.
3) A tagged student holds on to 'it's shoulders from behind to form a train.
4) When the train reaches 4 people it splits into two trains of 2 that each go off to tag other students; this repeats whenever a train reaches 4, and the game ends when the last remaining student is caught.
풀(또는 지우개), 책상, TV 화면(문제 PPT)

1) Face your partner and place one object to grab, such as a glue stick or pencil case, in the middle of the desk.
2) Show a learning quiz question with 2–3 answer choices on the screen and let students think of the answer.
3) When the teacher calls body parts like head, shoulders, belly or knees, students place both hands on that part; when the teacher shouts 'Grab it!', the student who grabs the object in the middle first gets priority.
4) The student who grabbed it first whispers the answer to their partner, and scores a point if it is correct.
Glue stick (or eraser), desks, TV screen (quiz slides)
단어 카드 세트, 바구니, 칠판 마커, 책상

1) Make word cards for four category topics chosen by the teacher, 3 matching cards per topic; each student blindly draws 3 cards and places them face down on the desk.
2) At the start signal, students walk around and play rock-paper-scissors with friends from other groups.
3) The winner checks one of the loser's cards and takes it, then hands over one card they do not need. Players in the same group cannot trade with each other.
4) A student who first completes a set of 3 cards on the same topic writes the topic's first letter under their group number on the board; the group wins when it completes all four topics.
Word card set, basket, board markers, desks

1) Randomly hand out cards listing unique abilities such as Angel, Zombie, Ice, Charge, Turtle, Reflect and Phoenix to the team members.
2) Play by basic dodgeball rules, but activate special abilities once or continuously according to your own power.
3) The Shield player is not out when hit but cannot attack and defends teammates; the Turtle survives indefinitely if hit on the back. Ice freezes the whole opposing team for 10 seconds, and Charge may enter the opposing side and attack for 10 seconds.
4) The game ends when every player on one team is out.

1) Students sit with their groups, and the teacher plays rock-paper-scissors against the whole class.
2) Students who win move to 1st base (the playground-side window); those who lose or tie stay in their seats.
3) If the student on 1st base wins the next round, they advance one base at a time to 2nd base (back of the classroom) and then 3rd base (hallway-side window).
4) A student who wins once more from 3rd base and reaches home marks a scoring circle on the board under their group number and returns to their seat.
Blackboard, board markers, desks and chairs
교실 술래잡기 피구 (토끼 잡는 거북이 놀이)
안전 폼볼 2개, 타이머, 창문 보호용 우드락, 교실 책상 및 의자

1) With everyone's head down, secretly tap students to pick 2 turtles ('it') and 2 secret Dragon Kings; the 2 turtles carry foam balls and throw at the fleeing rabbits around the classroom.
2) A rabbit that is hit must sit down on the spot and can be revived when a secret Dragon King sneaks over and touches them.
3) A rabbit who catches a ball thrown by a turtle directly is not out, and may roll the ball far away and flee.
4) When the 3-minute timer ends, the rabbits win if 10 or more rabbits survive; the turtles win if there are fewer than 10, or if both Dragon Kings are eliminated.
2 safety foam balls, timer, foam board for window protection, classroom desks and chairs

1) Divide the class into two sections; one or two representatives from each team sit at front desks with a golden-bell board and a board marker.
2) Looking at the word shown on the screen, all the other students in the section express it using only gestures and movements, without speaking.
3) The seated representatives infer the answer from their teammates' gestures and write it on the board; when one team finishes first, the other team gets 10 extra seconds and then both answers are revealed at the same time.
4) The team that answers correctly records a point on the board, and the next set of students takes over.
Golden-bell board (or sketchbook/notebook), board markers, desks, chairs
활동 카드 세트(선대칭도형 카드 및 일반 카드)

1) Each group randomly draws 5 cards mixed with thief cards (cards that are not line-symmetric figures) and arranges them on the desk.
2) When the round starts, members go in numerical order starting from number 1 to a neighboring group and draw one card.
3) After bringing a card back, check whether it is a thief, then act convincingly so the next person doesn't notice, and place it back on the desk.
4) When every group member has drawn once and the round ends, the group that has collected the most thief cards wins.
Activity card set (line-symmetric figure cards and regular cards)

1) Choose 2 Stone Ghosts ('it') and 3 King Stones; everyone else becomes a stone and lies with their head down on the desk.
2) While the Stone Ghosts observe the students for 10 seconds and then step out into the hallway, the King Stones quickly swap seats and coats with other students and put their heads down again.
3) The returning Stone Ghosts get 40 seconds to stand and look around the classroom to find the hidden King Stones.
4) The Stone Ghosts have 2 chances in total to point; a pointed-out student raises their head if correct or shakes it if wrong.

1) Arrange chairs in a circle, remove one chair, and have one 'it' player stand in the middle.
2) 'It' raises both hands high above the head and plays rock-paper-scissors with all the seated students.
3) Only the students who lost stand up and quickly move to find an empty seat and sit down.
4) The student left without a seat becomes the next 'it' and continues the game with a new condition (losers, tied players, etc.).

1) Push the desks to the back and sides to make space, divide the class into three teams (the Three Kingdoms), and choose a king for each team.
2) Students play seated and throw the ball at opposing teams to hit them; the king cannot be eliminated but is not allowed to throw.
3) Students who are hit and out can stand at the front of their team and act as defenders, batting away incoming balls with their arms only.
4) When all of a team's members except the king are out, or the king is out, that team is absorbed into the attacking team; the team that finally unifies all the kingdoms wins.

1) With everyone lying head-down on their desks, the teacher taps backs to choose 4 Mafia members and shows the Mafia mission on the screen.
2) The Mafia secretly carry out the given mission, while all students walk around the classroom for 2 minutes observing and suspecting each other.
3) When time is up, students sit down and nominate 8 suspected Mafia members (twice the number of Mafia), who are called to the front.
4) The nominated students reveal their identities one by one; the citizens win if all 4 Mafia are found, and the Mafia win if even 1 is missed.
Screen/slides to show missions, desks, chairs

1) Each group chooses a 2–5 syllable chant and a unique 3–4 beat movement.
2) At the start signal, students walk around the classroom performing their group's chant and movement, and play rock-paper-scissors when they meet someone from another team.
3) The loser is absorbed into the winning team and immediately switches to that team's chant and movement.
4) After a set time, teams gather to check which teams survive, and play continues until the whole class is unified under one team's chant and movement.

1) Divide the class into two teams, add the teacher's name to each team's roster, fold up name slips for the students, and distinguish the teams with pinnies or sashes.
2) Each student randomly draws one slip bearing a name from the opposing team; the student who draws the slip with the teacher's name returns it to the teacher, and the student named on that slip becomes that team's 'Invisible Person'.
3) For 2 minutes, students meet opposing players and play rock-paper-scissors; only the winner checks the loser's slip to collect clues.
4) When time is up, teammates compare the lists they have gathered and make a final deduction of who the other team's Invisible Person is.

1) Turn all desks to face inward to form a circle, then choose two detectives and send them out of the room for a moment.
2) While the detectives are out, secretly choose one leader inside the classroom.
3) When the detectives step into the middle of the room, the leader starts various body movements in time with the music while everyone else copies the leader's moves.
4) The detectives watch the students' movements and, after the music ends, try to work out who the leader is.

1) Students follow only the commands the leader gives with 'Simon says' (Garasadae) attached, and must never move for commands without it.
2) Even if students make a mistake, they are not eliminated; they honestly acknowledge their own error and keep taking part.
3) The leader tricks students with a variety of moves and wordplay, such as attention, clapping and sparkling hands.
4) At the end of the set time, the game wraps up by finding the students who never made a mistake.
Group Speed Charades (Act It Out Together)

1) Pick 1–2 guessers by lottery or nomination and send them to the video-call waiting room so they cannot see the prompt word.
2) Show the remaining students the prompt (e.g., gorilla, spider, a proverb) via screen share, then bring the guessers back into the meeting.
3) On the signal, all students act out the word at the same time using only gestures and facial expressions, with no voice.
4) The guessers watch their classmates' movements on screen and type their answer in the chat to guess the word.

1) Players stand facing the leader and agree to follow a command only when it begins with 'Garasadae' (Simon says).
2) The leader gives commands such as 'Garasadae, raise your right hand,' and players perform the movement.
3) Anyone who moves on a command without 'Garasadae' is out and kneels or sits down.
4) The leader mixes in fake commands such as 'lower it,' and the last player still standing who has not been fooled wins.

1) For the 2-person mission, face each other, point one hand up and one hand down, and clasp hands crosswise.
2) Without letting go, rotate your arms and bodies until you return to a normal handhold.
3) For the group mission, 3 or more players grab different people's hands at random, then untangle into a circle by passing through hand-made gates and twisting their bodies.
4) The mission succeeds if all knots are undone within the time limit without anyone letting go.

1) Arrange classroom desks in 4 long rows to form a snail-shaped path and split the class into two teams.
2) Both teams start from opposite ends at a brisk walk and play Rock-Paper-Scissors when they meet.
3) The loser sits on a desk and the winner keeps advancing; the losing team's next runner starts right away, and a seated player is revived when a teammate touches them as they pass.
4) A team wins by reaching the opposite end and also winning Rock-Paper-Scissors against the last waiting player.

1) Both the tagger and runners may move only along the lines painted on the gym floor; the tagger holds a pinnie in hand to stand out.
2) The tagger moves along the lines and chases the runners.
3) When the tagger touches a runner, roles swap, and the new tagger slowly counts 5 seconds in place before chasing.
4) Stepping off the lines or jumping over a line is a foul.
스피드 스택스 컵 4세트(색상별), 콩주머니 4개, 책상 및 의자
Curling Cups (Bean Bag and Cup Desktop Battle)

1) Push 9 desks together in the middle of the room to form the arena, and place each team's desk 3 steps away.
2) Teams take turns tossing a bean bag onto the center desks.
3) If the bean bag lands and stays on the desks, place one of your team's stacking cups there and retrieve the bean bag; knocking an opponent's cup off removes it from the arena.
4) When one team uses all its cups or time runs out, the team with the most cups on the desks wins.
4 color-coded sets of stacking cups, 4 bean bags, desks and chairs
Random Attendance Sheet (Guess Who Wrote It)

1) Students privately fill out attendance sheets with questions about themselves (favorite food, season, subject, etc.) and hand them to the host.
2) The host shuffles the sheets, draws one, and reads out its contents one item at a time.
3) Players guess whose sheet it is and raise their hands to name the person; if it is your own sheet, you must pretend not to know.
4) After a correct answer, draw a new sheet and keep going to get to know your classmates.

1) Warm up lightly by walking and jogging in place.
2) First move: 60 seconds of Go-Back walking, stepping forward and back while reaching the arms overhead; second move: 60 seconds of side jumps, hopping left and right.
3) Third move: skate steps, traveling side to side while touching the opposite ankle.
4) Finish with a wide-arm side walk, stepping left and right while raising both arms overhead and lowering them.
다양한 색상 및 크기의 병뚜껑, 종이컵, 종이테이프, 책상

1) Set up paper-cup goals and taped square target zones on desks to play five bottle-cap mini sports: soccer, basketball, bowling, color pool, and square curling.
2) Flick or roll bottle caps with your fingers to land them in the paper-cup goal or reach the designated target zone.
3) In the pool version, hit your opponent's caps in rainbow color order to knock them off the table.
4) In curling and bowling, control power and spin to score points or knock away opposing caps.
Bottle caps of various colors and sizes, paper cups, masking tape, desks
번호가 적힌 뽑기 막대(또는 주사위), 칠판, 분필/마커

1) Write the numbers of 6 zones in the classroom (corners and sides) on the board, along with words for students' interests such as food or hobbies.
2) On the signal, everyone walks to the zone number they want during a 5-second countdown.
3) The teacher randomly draws one stick numbered 1–6; students standing in that zone are out and return to their seats, and that zone is crossed out with an X.
4) Repeat the rounds, and the students in the last surviving zone win.
Numbered draw sticks (or a die), blackboard, chalk/markers
플래그 풋볼 벨트(4색 태그벨트), 라바콘 4개, 원마커 4색
Color Tail Tag (4-Team Flag Belt Battle)

1) Mark team zones on the field with 4 colors of cones, split into 4 teams, and have each student wear a flag belt in their team color.
2) On the signal, run freely around the field and pull flags (tails) from opposing teams' belts.
3) Only one flag may be pulled at a time and must be taken to your team's cone zone before you can pull another; a student who loses both flags rests outside the field.
4) When time is up, the team with the most flags collected at its cone wins.
Flag football belts (4 colors), 4 cones, spot markers in 4 colors

1) Line up 3 desks of equal height and tape 4 paper cups at each end to make the arena.
2) Split into two teams, line up behind your cups, and prepare as many ping-pong balls as there are cups per team.
3) Teams alternate rolling a ball across the desks toward the opposing cups; a ball that lands in a cup claims that spot and stays, while a miss or a ball landing in an already occupied cup is taken back.
4) The first team to get a ball into every one of the opponent's cups wins.
Desks, ping-pong balls, paper cups, tape
Overpass Game (Consecutive Passes Over Defenders' Heads)

1) Mark 4 long zones with a line marker or cones and place half of each team (A and B) alternately in the zones.
2) The starting team throws the ball over a defender's head to a teammate one zone away, and the receiver continues the same way.
3) Completing 5 consecutive passes over opposing defenders' heads scores 1 point; if a defender knocks down or steals the ball, or it hits the floor or goes out of bounds, possession switches.
4) The team with more points when time ends, or the first to reach the target score, wins.
Cones or line marker, dodgeball (or soft ball)
점수 피구 (맞아도 아웃 없는 차등 점수제)

1) Make a large circular arena with cones or lines and assign an attacking team (outside the circle) and a defending team (inside).
2) Players who are hit do not leave the circle; everyone keeps playing for the set time.
3) The attackers score by hitting defenders: a player wearing a pinnie is worth 3 points and one without is worth 1; for upper grades, numbered pinnies (2, 3, 4, 9, etc.) can give that many points.
4) After a set time (e.g., 5 minutes) the teams switch roles, and the team with the higher total score wins.

1) Mark a circular arena with cones; the attacking team stands outside and the defending team inside.
2) Defenders form pairs (or groups of 4) and line up like a train, each holding the waist clothing of the person in front.
3) In the basic version the front player is a shield who is not out when hit, but the rear player is out immediately when hit; once the rear player leaves, the remaining front player is out if hit.
4) Count the survivors after a set time or measure how long it takes to eliminate everyone, then switch roles and compare.

Dice Run Relay (Circle the Turnaround Cone as Many Times as the Roll)

1) Split the class into two teams, set the running order, and mark the start and turnaround points with cones.
2) The first runner throws a fabric die high overhead from the start line and reads the number that lands face up.
3) Carrying the die, sprint to the turnaround, circle it as many times as the number rolled, then return and safely hand the die to the next runner.
4) The first team whose last runner finishes circling the turnaround and returns wins.
2 fabric dice, cones (start and turnaround markers), jump ropes (for variations)
피구공(또는 소프트볼/주먹야구공), 베이스 마커(접시콘 또는 원마커)

1) Split the class into batting and fielding teams and set up the batter's box, first, second and third base, home, and foul lines.
2) A batter tosses a dodgeball up with one hand, lightly punches it into fair territory, and runs the bases.
3) Reaching first base scores 1 point, second 2, third 3, and home 5; fielders get runners out by catching fly balls or tagging them directly while holding the ball.
4) After every batter on the batting team has hit once, add up the total score and switch roles.
Dodgeball (or soft ball / fist-baseball ball), base markers (cones or spot markers)

1) Use cones to mark an outer circle and a small inner circle to form a donut-shaped arena, and split into two teams.
2) One representative of the attacking team stands in the small center circle, the defending team enters the donut ring area, and the rest of the attackers stand around the outside of the outer circle.
3) The outside attackers score 1 point each time they complete a pass to the teammate in the center; defenders bat away or block incoming throws and hurl any ball that enters the ring far outside to delay scoring.
4) After a set time (e.g., 3 minutes) the teams switch roles, and final scores are compared.

Circle Dodgeball (Step-by-Step: Dodging, One-Person Dodgeball, Circle Game)

1) Make a large circular arena with cones and practice the basic dodgeball skills of throwing, dodging, and passing step by step.
2) In the main game, 2–3 throwers stand outside the circle and all remaining students stand inside as dodgers.
3) The outside throwers pass and throw the ball to hit the dodgers inside; a student who is hit leaves the circle.
4) When the number of students left inside drops to the set number (2–4), those remaining become the outside throwers and teams swap roles to repeat.

1) Set up the bases (spot markers or cones), split into two teams, and have a pitcher ready to roll the ball.
2) The kicker kicks the ball rolled by the pitcher, runs the bases, and scores by reaching home.
3) Fielders can get a runner out by throwing the ball to the base before the runner arrives or by tagging the runner while holding the ball; catching a kick before it touches the ground is a fly out and the runner must return to the original base.
4) Four balls send the kicker to first base, and three accumulated strikes or fouls make the kicker out.
Kickball (soccer ball/volleyball), bases (spot markers or cones)
Challenge: Learning the Basics of the Fosbury Flop

1) Set up the high jump mat and takeoff spot, and begin step by step with mat landing and approach-step practice without a bar.
2) Run toward the high jump mat using a curved approach.
3) Plant one foot hard at the takeoff spot and launch your body into the air.
4) Arch back in the air so your back faces the mat and land on it.
High jump mat, cones (to guide the approach steps), takeoff board

1) Run up over a fixed distance, building speed as you approach.
2) Take off precisely from one foot without stepping on or over the takeoff line.
3) After the air phase, land safely in the sand pit with both knees bent softly.
4) Measure the distance from the takeoff line to the nearest point touched by any part of the body.
Takeoff board, sand pit (long jump pit)

Flying Disc Basics (Grip, Throw, Catch, Pivot)

1) Learn the backhand grip (control/power grip) and the forehand grip.
2) Throw toward the target with a wrist snap, keeping the disc parallel to the ground.
3) Catch chest-high throws with a pancake catch using both hands from above and below, and catch face-high throws by covering the disc with both hands.
4) After catching, keep one foot planted as a pivot foot and connect to the next pass.

3) Team members take turns throwing in order, and the total number of successful catches decides the winner.
4) As a variation, runners from teams A and B can face off in the center zone, competing to grab the disc first.

2) Stage 1: with feet together, jump to the beat in the order front, left x3, right x3, then front again; when the person ahead moves to the third line or square, the next person starts from the first square.
3) Stage 2: jump out with feet apart to the sides; Stage 3: two lines face each other and start in an alternating pattern.
4) Stage 4: four students start at once from four directions, jumping to the beat without their paths overlapping.

Movement Language and Expression Game (Find the Leader)

2) Choose a guesser, then secretly pick one group member as the 'leader'; while the guesser stands in the middle and observes, the others quickly copy the leader's non-locomotor movements without being noticed.
3) The guesser tries to find out who is leading the movements within the time limit.
4) In the following locomotor activity, the other students follow the leader's path and steps like shadows.

3) On 'same words, same action,' players shout the direction and jump that way together; on 'same words, opposite action,' they shout the direction while jumping the opposite way.

3) Swing your arms forcefully from back to front and lean your upper body forward as you jump strongly.
4) Land on both feet at the same time, leaning your upper body forward to gain distance.

1) Hollow-Body Leg Lower: lie on your back with arms, shoulders, and bent legs lifted off the floor; slowly extend legs out on a 5-count and return without touching heels down.
