4) Use as a quick warm-up or brain-break and rotate partners in a mini-tournament format.

1) Arrange desks in groups of four facing each other, fold paper into 8 sections, and write 8 words to act out.
2) Determine turns by rock-paper-scissors; the presenter tears off an end word and acts it out silently.
3) Teammates raise hands to guess the answer, and whoever guesses correctly becomes the next presenter.
4) Finger count or initial letter hints can be given when difficult, continuing until all teammates finish all words.
1/4 sheet of A4 paper per student, pencils
반대로 핸들 돌리기 붕붕붕 부릉부릉 교실체조

1) Sit at the classroom desk and hold both hands out as if gripping a car steering wheel.
2) When the teacher shouts "Bung-bung-bung!", students respond together with "Bureung-bureung!" and focus.
3) When the teacher commands "Right!", students turn the wheel right while leaning their body to the left in opposite coordination.
4) Once mastered, add extra commands like "Forward" (lean back), "Brake" (lean forward), and "Speed Bump" (seat jump) for reaction training.
Inner-Outer Circle Passing Balloon Strike Game

1) Students form two concentric circles with an inner circle of 6 players and an outer circle of 8 players standing within arms reach.
2) Inner players pass a balloon among themselves while outer players pass a ball around their own circle.
3) An outer player succeeds and swaps positions with an inner player if they strike and drop the inner team's balloon.
4) With more participants, add two balls and two balloons or reverse the passing direction dynamically.
가위바위보 부족 연맹 국가의 탄생 놀이
Rock-Paper-Scissors Tribe Federation: Birth of a Nation

1) All students start as individual cavemen, play best-of-three rock-paper-scissors with peers, and the loser attaches behind the winner as a train.
2) When a group grows to 4-5 students, they form a tribe and create a unique tribal chant and signature gesture together.
3) Tribes meet, perform their chants, and engage in survival rock-paper-scissors where the losing tribe merges into the winning tribe's federation.
4) The game progresses with 1-on-1 matches between federations until the entire class is unified into a single nation.
말랑한 폼볼 1개, 책상 및 의자 세트

1) Desks are arranged facing each other in two team rows with boys and girls sitting alternately side by side.
2) Attackers stand in the center aisle and throw a soft foam ball toward the seated opposing team.
3) A girl is out if hit by a girl's throw and a boy is out if hit by a boy's throw, while players hit by the opposite gender are safe, allowing neighbors of the other gender to extend their arms as bodyguards.
4) Standing up or hiding underneath the desk counts as a foul, and the team with more surviving players wins.
1 soft foam ball, desks and chairs
Whole Class Circle Invisible Chair Challenge

1) Arrange classroom chairs in a tight circle facing sideways after clearing the central space.
2) On cue, all students lie back simultaneously using the person behind them as a lap pillow.
3) The teacher gradually pulls out all chairs one by one, leaving students supporting each other.
4) Maintain the human-bridge circular formation without chairs for the target countdown to complete the mission.
감정 공감 원형 의자 바꾸기 놀이

1) Arrange chairs in a circle with one less chair than the total number of students and place one 'it' player in the center.
2) The tagger picks an emotion word displayed on screen and shares a personal story of why they felt that emotion.
3) Classmates ask "Why?" and only those who empathize with the shared experience must stand up and dash to a different empty chair.
4) The student left without a seat becomes the next tagger, and becoming 'it' three times requires a fun short talent show.
오른쪽! 왼쪽! 흔들어 (원형 방향 반응 점프 놀이)

1) Students stand in a large circle and hold hands with their peers on both sides.
2) The teacher calls out directional commands (Right, Left, Forward, Backward, In-place, Shake), and students jump in unison while keeping hands held.
3) Without eliminations, the goal is to maintain the circle formation and rhythm without tripping or letting go of hands.
4) For variation, increase the tempo gradually or apply the 'opposite rule' where students jump in the reverse direction of the call.

1) Form small table groups with assigned player numbers while the facilitator prepares a covered word card list in the corner.
2) Player one from each team rushes to check the first hidden prompt and acts it out silently using only body motions.
3) Once teammates guess correctly, the next player runs to whisper the answer to the proctor and receives the next prompt to act out.
4) The team whose members successfully guess all prompts and complete the final group chant mission first wins the challenge.
Desks, chairs, prompt sheet, folder binder
학생 1인당 의자 1개 및 책상 1개, OX 퀴즈용 손피켓 1개(선택)

1) Students start by lying flat on the floor beside their desks.
2) Players play rock-paper-scissors or answer quizzes against the teacher, moving up one level upon success: sitting on the floor, sitting on the chair, standing on the chair, and sitting on the desk.
3) When reaching the top desk level and raising both arms shouting hooray, the player scores 1 point, and then reverses the sequence down to the floor to earn another point.
4) Rules can be modified by altering winning conditions (e.g., tying or losing) or using cham-cham-cham mini-games to provide more opportunities.
1 desk and 1 chair per student, 1 OX paddle per student (optional)
주사위 1개, 종이 쪽지 8장 이상, 바구니 1개, 스케치북 1권, 연필/필기도구 1자루

1) Fold and cut paper into strips, write target words such as animals or objects on each, fold them, and place them into a basket.
2) A quiz presenter draws one paper strip in secret and rolls a die.
3) Depending on the roll (1-2 for body gestures, 3-4 for verbal clues, 5-6 for drawing), the presenter describes the word, and the first guesser earns 1 point and becomes the next presenter.
4) In pairs, add a 30-second time limit per word to compete on how many words can be solved within the time.
1 die, 8+ paper slips, 1 basket, 1 sketchpad, 1 pencil/pen
의자 1개 및 책상 1개(학생 1인당), 메트로놈 또는 배경 음악(선택)

1) The teacher stands at the front as the conductor while students sit upright at their individual classroom desks.
2) The conductor performs a continuous sequence of 4-beat body percussion actions (e.g., knee tap 4 times, clap 4 times, shoulder tap 4 times, head tap 4 times).
3) Students must not copy immediately, but must perform the conductor's previous movement one sequence behind while observing the conductor's new movement.
4) To increase difficulty, speed up the tempo, divide the 4 beats into 2-beat combinations, or invite proficient students to take over as conductors.
1 desk and 1 chair per student, metronome or background music (optional)

1) Students wear masks and stand or sit at their designated classroom desks maintaining personal distance.
2) The teacher explains the movement rules focusing on non-contact coordination and visual interaction.
3) Students perform target physical responses or coordination cues according to the teacher's signals.
4) The difficulty increases progressively by changing movement patterns and response speed without physical contact.
박자 맞춰 시차 따라하기 율동 놀이

1) Participants stand or sit comfortably facing the screen or leader with enough personal moving space.
2) The leader performs a specific body movement for four beats and transitions immediately to the next movement.
3) Students observe carefully and mirror the leader's previous movement exactly one sequence behind.
4) Increase the challenge by shortening the interval to three or two beats or rotating student leaders.

1) Two partners sit or stand facing each other and choose a reaction rule set such as block or tag.
2) Both players perform rock-paper-scissors simultaneously and instantly identify the outcome.
3) The winner immediately executes the attack action while the loser performs the required block or evasive maneuver.
4) Introduce variations like mental addition, reverse shout calls, or finger coordination for added complexity.
숨은 연주가 찾기 연기 관찰 놀이

1) A group steps into the hallway and secretly designates one member to only mime playing the recorder.
2) The group stands in front of the classroom and performs a learned tune together while the secret player pretends.
3) Seated classmates listen closely and observe players' finger movements, breath, and expressions to deduce the imposter.
4) The audience discusses in small groups to guess the hidden player, then positions are swapped for the next round.

1) Pair up students facing each other across a desk or standing face-to-face.
2) Choose one mode such as Cheers RPS, Lose-to-Win RPS, Quick Hand-Tag RPS, Addition RPS, or Toy-Hammer RPS.
3) Students compete to score points by shouting the outcome first, tagging the opponent's hand, or summing numbers faster.
4) Increase difficulty by inverting the verbal cues or switching attack and defense roles.
온라인 무궁화 꽃이 피었습니다 박수 챌린지
Zoom Red Light Green Light Clap Challenge

1) Students stand in front of their webcams facing the screen.
2) While the tagger turns away and chants the countdown phrase, players clap rhythmically in front and behind their body.
3) If a player moves when the tagger turns back, their count resets to zero; the first player to reach 30 claps and press the raise-hand button wins.
4) Add character pose missions such as Spider-Man or elephant stances during freeze moments to increase engagement.
Device with webcam and Zoom software
책상 9개, 의자 9개, 대형 스펀지 주사위 1개, 단계별 문제지

1) Arrange classroom desks in a horseshoe layout and place stage 1–9 quiz sheets at designated desks.
2) Roll a large die at the blackboard to jump directly to that stage and point to a question for the desk examiner.
3) Answering correctly advances the player to the next stage and scores a point, while answering incorrectly swaps roles with the examiner.
4) Clearing all stages allows rolling the die again, and the team with the highest accumulated score wins.
9 desks, 9 chairs, 1 large foam die, staged quiz sheets

1) Divide the class into two opposing teams holding hands in a circular formation, placing a paper cup on a chair between the end players.
2) At the start signal, the front player squeezes the next player's hand to send a tactile "electric pulse" down the line.
3) The moment the last player feels their hand squeezed, they snatch the cup off the chair, scoring a point for the faster team.
4) After each round, the end players rotate to the very front of the line so all students cycle through the grabbing position.
Head Shoulders Knees Forbidden Word Warm-up

1) Students stand by their desks and prepare along with the song Head Shoulders Knees and Toes.
2) In each round, omit saying specific body parts aloud (e.g., verse 1 silences 'head', verse 2 'shoulders') while still performing the movements.
3) Students score points or remain in the game by staying silent on the forbidden words without messing up the choreography.
4) Increase difficulty by silencing multiple words simultaneously or speeding up the tempo.

1) Divide the class into two teams (Vest team and No-vest team), push all chairs under desks, and line up along opposite walls.
2) Only the team called by the teacher shouts 'One step!' and moves exactly one step in any direction like chess pieces.
3) If a player touches an opponent upon moving, the tagged student is infected, switches vests, and restarts from the other wall.
4) The game continues with shifting team sizes until one team successfully infects all opponents to win.
가위바위보 릴레이 달리기와 후프 뜀뛰기 놀이
Rock-Paper-Scissors Running and Hoop Jumping Relay

1) Set up a curved track using cones and action hoops on the field, divide the class into two teams wearing vests, and line them up at opposite ends.
2) On the start signal, the first runners from each team move forward—sprinting through the cone zone and two-foot hopping through the hoop zone.
3) When opponents meet, they stop and play rock-paper-scissors; the winner continues advancing while the loser leaves the track, allowing their team's next runner to sprint out immediately.
4) A point is scored when a player reaches the opponent's final hoop or cone, and movement patterns can be modified into single-leg hops or zigzag running.
30 marker cones, 20 action hoops, 20 team pinnies

1) Students stand in a circle holding the edge of the parachute and walk or run in the specified direction together.
2) Raise and lower the parachute smoothly or quickly on the teacher's cue to understand airflow and rhythm.
3) When a color is called, students holding that color dash underneath to an open spot on the opposite side.
4) Step inward together to create an umbrella or mushroom dome to sit inside, or work together to pop small balls high into the air.
개인 풍선 제어 및 모둠 풍선 띄우기 놀이
Individual and Cooperative Balloon Control Challenge

1) Each student tosses a balloon above their spot marker, performs a body turn or jump, and safely catches it.
2) Tap the balloon consecutively using designated body parts like headers, thighs, and foot-taps without letting it drop.
3) In groups of 4 to 5, hold hands in a circle and keep a single balloon afloat using only hands, arms, or heads.
4) If hands disconnect or the balloon touches the floor, the team sits down, and the longest-surviving group wins.

1) Teams line up single-file behind the starting marker, with a target basket placed at the far end of the court.
2) The front player twists at the waist and passes the ball sideways to the player behind, then sprints to the back of the line to extend it.
3) In later rounds, raise the difficulty by alternating overhead and between-the-legs passes (over-under-over-under), or by facing a partner and throwing and catching.
4) Players must not walk or run while holding the ball; the first team to place the ball in the basket from outside the marked area and finish with a team high-five wins.
모둠 콘 타워 집 지키기 배틀

1) Each team builds a cone tower in their zone and marks a defensive boundary line that defenders cannot cross.
2) Attackers throw dodgeballs to knock down the opposing cone tower while defenders block incoming balls outside the line.
3) Introduce a rebuilding rule allowing designated repairers to rebuild fallen towers while teammates protect and retrieve balls.
4) When the timer runs out, the team that has protected more standing cone towers claims the victory.

1) Line up 4-5 desks in a row with a plastic collection basket placed on the final desk, and form teams behind each start line.
2) On the starting signal, the first player throws a ping pong ball to skip and bounce consecutively across the desk surfaces.
3) If the ball successfully lands into the end basket, the team scores 1 point, and the thrower retrieves the ball and passes it to the next teammate.
4) Play as a timed relay race to see which team scores the most balls, or widen the spacing between desks to increase difficulty.
12 desks, 3+ ping pong balls, 3 plastic baskets
플라잉디스크 팀당 2개(총 6개), 점보 스택스 컵 팀당 11개(총 33개), 원마커 3개

1) Set up ten jumbo stacking cups in a pyramid with a bonus disc placed atop the farthest cup, and mark shooting lines with spot markers.
2) The first thrower from each team launches a flying disc toward the target cups from behind the marker.
3) If a cup is knocked down, the thrower retrieves both the fallen cup and disc, stacks the cup at the base, and passes the disc to the next runner.
4) Knocking down the bonus cup grants an extra disc to speed up throws, and the first team to retrieve all their cups wins.
Flying discs 6 pcs, jumbo stacking cups 33 pcs, spot markers 3 pcs
플라잉디스크 팀당 1개(총 3개), 고깔콘 10개, 번호 원마커 16개(단계별 각 4개)

1) Divide the court into Levels 1 through 4 using cones and place numbered spot markers corresponding to each zone.
2) The first runner enters Level 1 while a teammate at the starting line throws a flying disc toward them.
3) Catching it cleanly allows the runner to call 'Stop' to take a level marker and return, or call 'Go' to advance to the next level.
4) Dropping the disc or catching it outside the zone results in zero points, and the team collecting the highest total score wins.
Flying discs 3 pcs, cones 10 pcs, numbered spot markers 16 pcs
숫자 원형 마커 수십 개, 콩주머니 팀당 3개 이상, 손 소독제 1개

1) Numbered spots representing fish are spread out by distance and team waiting/throwing lines are marked.
2) Players from each team take turns throwing beanbags three times toward target number spots from the throwing zone.
3) A team captures a marker if their beanbag rests on it, earning base points plus bonus points (Full Boat, Rainbow, Triple).
4) If multiple beanbags touch the same marker all fail, and players can push opponent bags away as a strategic variation.
Numbered circular markers, beanbags (at least 3 per team), hand sanitizer
점보 스택스 무한 높이 쌓기 도전
점보 스택스 105개 이상(또는 종이컵 다수), 안전 사다리 1대

1) Divide students into groups and distribute an equal number of jumbo stacking cups across team stations.
2) Teammates collaborate to build the tallest possible tower using vertical single-column, pyramid, or circular interlocking methods.
3) The group that builds the highest stable tower or reaches the targeted height without collapsing wins.
4) Can be adapted into a classroom challenge using paper cups or a relay format where runners place one cup at a time.
Jumbo stacking cups (105+ pcs) or large paper cups, safety stepladder

1) Place one chair as the throne at the front of the classroom and have all students sit in their groups starting at the lowest rank of 'Cheonmin'.
2) Students play rock-paper-scissors within their group to advance to 'Pyeongmin', then winners move to the front to compete against each other to become 'Jungin' and finally 'Yangban'.
3) The Yangban challenges the reigning King seated on the throne (the teacher initially), and winning makes them the new King who sits on the throne and has their name recorded on the board.
4) Defeated Kings or challengers drop back to the Cheonmin rank to restart from group matches, and the student who defends the throne the most times within the time limit wins.
1 chair, blackboard and chalk (or board marker)

1) Prepare table tennis balls marked with stars (1-7) and numbers (1-7) in egg cartons at each team base, and players randomly draw one ball.
2) Players run into the court to tag opponents; matching types compare numbers (1 higher wins, 1 beats 7), while hunters (numbers) only lose to the matching star number.
3) Winners take the defeated player's ball back to their egg carton, while eliminated players return to base to relay scouted information to active teammates.
4) The team that first captures all seven opposing star balls (Dragon Balls) and places them onto the center chair wins the game.
28 table tennis balls, 2 egg cartons, 4 cones, 1 chair
책상 6개, 작은 책상 2개, 미니 플라잉디스크 4개, 색깔 플라스틱 컵 16개

1) Line up six desks to form a curling track, divide the end into 1-2-3 point scoring zones, and prepare colored cups for each team.
2) Players from each team take turns sliding mini flying discs across the desk surface toward the scoring zones.
3) Place your team's colored cup on the zone where the disc stops, knocking out opponents' cups or accumulating higher points to win.
4) Modify the game by allowing consecutive slides or stacking cups to adjust difficulty.
6 standard desks, 2 small desks, 4 mini flying discs, 16 colored plastic cups

1) Arrange chairs in a circle with one less than the number of students, and assign each child one of four fruit names.
2) The tagger in the center waits for the class chant and calls out one or more fruit names.
3) Students assigned to that fruit must get up and race to an empty chair while the tagger also tries to take a seat, leaving one new tagger.
4) When the tagger shouts "Fruit Basket!", all students must get up and swap seats simultaneously.
Chairs (one fewer than the total number of students)

1) Divide the rectangular court into two halves, draw a center circle inside each half, and place an outer thrower and an inside spy in each opponent zone.
2) Players start the game by passing the ball between the outer thrower and the inner spy to attack opponent field players from multiple angles.
3) Players hit by the dodgeball are eliminated to the opponent outer boundary as throwers, while the inner spy inside the circle never gets eliminated even if hit.
4) Spies cannot step outside their designated circle nor grab rolling balls outside the boundary, and the team that eliminates all opponent fielders wins.

1) Divide a square field into four quadrants marked A-B-A-B clockwise, split each team into two groups, and position them in diagonally opposite zones.
2) If player numbers are high, assign outer throwers, and start the match with players throwing balls across borders into adjacent opponent zones.
3) When hit, an eliminated player moves to the outer boundary located directly to the right of their current zone to act as an outside thrower.
4) Enhance gameplay by permitting players to cross diagonally between friendly zones, and the team that eliminates all opponent infielders wins.
1-2 dodgeballs, 16 disc cones (or field line marker)

1) Split players into two teams with outer throwers and designate one player in each infield as the 'Invincible Defender'.
2) The Invincible Defender actively blocks incoming dodgeballs using their hands or a handheld shield to guard vulnerable teammates.
3) Under base rules the defender never gets out, but under shield rules getting hit directly on the body eliminates them and transfers the shield to a teammate.
4) All regular fielders must be eliminated first, and the opposing team secures victory only when the last remaining Invincible Defender is struck out.
1 dodgeball, 2 shields (foam pads, mats, or strike shields), line marker

1) Teams line up maintaining intervals and each runner places a marker cone on their head.
2) Roll the dice at the start and run around the designated turning point based on the roll (e.g., odd numbers for near, even numbers for far).
3) If the cone falls, the runner must return to the start or turning point to put it back on before continuing to tag the next player.
4) Rules can be modified by turning the cone upside down indoors or sprinting without the cone when rolling even numbers.

1) Partners stand 2 meters apart at the starting line and designate a turning point such as a post or tree.
2) Partners play rock-paper-scissors, and the winner takes large leaping steps toward the target (variations allow rock=1 step, scissors=2 steps, paper=3 steps).
3) After touching the turning point first, players continue playing rock-paper-scissors to advance back toward the starting point.
4) The player who successfully returns to the starting position and sits down first wins the game.
고층 아파트 층수 누적 손쌓기 놀이
High-Rise Apartment Hand Stacking Math Game

1) A group of 3 to 6 players gathers in a circle and sets a target cumulative score such as 50 points.
2) Players chant "Apartment, Apartment" while stacking hands alternately, and the designated caller announces a target floor number (e.g., between 5 and 15).
3) Starting from the bottom hand, players pull out their hands one by one to count up, and the person whose hand matches the called floor earns that number of points.
4) Players mentally add their points after each round, and the first player to reach the target cumulative score wins.

1) Two or three players face each other and learn the designated points for each hand sign (Scissors=1, Rock=2, Paper=3 / variant: finger counts 2, 0, 5).
2) Players call out "Rock-Paper-Scissors" simultaneously and quickly add up the point values shown by everyone's hands.
3) The first player to correctly shout the total sum while raising both hands high wins the round point.
4) The game can be varied by multiplying the values instead of adding, and the first player to score 3 to 5 points wins.

1) Form two teams standing in line while holding hands, with the first runner holding a baton or ball.
2) On the starting whistle, each runner sprints along the path curving around the linked teammates and opposing line.
3) Teammates narrow their stance to shorten their runner's path while stretching wide to lengthen the opponent's path, scoring when the last baton is returned to the basket first.
4) Modify the relay by adding ball dribbling, wearing a backpack, or setting a penalty if hands disconnect three times.
2인 패스 연계 및 전진 슛팅 훈련
Two-Player Pass and Run Shooting Drill

1) Set up two cone lines facing a soccer goal and assign a rotating goalkeeper.
2) The lead runner passes to a partner on the side and immediately sprints forward toward the front cone.
3) The partner returns a leading pass into space, and the running player strikes a first-time shot on goal.
4) Switch passing sides to practice both feet and rotate students through the goalkeeper position.

1) Lay out three hula hoops in a straight line increasing in distance towards the soccer goal.
2) The first thrower steps into hoop level 1 and tosses the flying disc towards the goal net.
3) Upon completing each stage, the player advances to hoops 2 and 3 to attempt goals, scoring 1 team point per successful throw.
4) Once a player completes all three attempts, all discs are gathered and the next teammate takes a turn to tally scores.
6 flying discs, 6 hula hoops, 4 cones, 1 soccer goal
노드리블 패스 연결 초등 변형 넷볼

1) Divide students into two teams wearing pinnies (4–6 per side) and begin play from center court with a pass.
2) The ball carrier is strictly prohibited from dribbling or walking and may only pivot to pass to open teammates.
3) Non-ball-carrying players continuously sprint into open passing lanes to advance the ball towards the basket.
4) Scoring occurs when a shot passes through the ring; an airball or intercepted pass results in an immediate turnover.
1 netball, 12 team vests, 2 portable netball hoops
패드민턴 라켓 12개, 탱탱볼 3개, 풍선 3개, 책상용 네트 3개, 점수판 3개, 책상 30개

1) Line up ten desks to form a table tennis court, install a net in the center, and assign 6 players per court (2v2 with 2 student referees).
2) Using padminton paddles, the server bounces the bouncy ball on their side and then over the net onto the receiver's side.
3) During rallies, players must return the ball directly over the net after a single bounce on their table half.
4) Games are played to 7 points, after which referees rotate in as active players, or switch to 1v1 singles.
12 padminton paddles, 3 bouncy balls, 3 balloons, 3 table nets, 3 flip scoreboards, 30 desks

1) Setup: Divide students into teams of 3 to 4 on each side of the net, with every player holding a Boundaroon racket.
2) Gameplay: Serve the foam ball and pass it between teammates 2 to 3 times before bouncing it over the net to the opposing side.
3) Scoring: A team scores a point when the opponents fail to return the ball or drop it, and the team reaching the goal score first wins.
4) Variation: Practice individual bouncing, flipping the racket between bounces, or paired rallies before moving to full net games.
12 Boundaroon rackets, 6 foam balls, 1 badminton net set

1) Mark a rectangular zone using cones and divide students into two teams wearing pinnies.
2) The attacking team passes the ball without dribbling while the defenders attempt to intercept airborne passes.
3) Players call out cumulative pass numbers to score 1 point each, and the first team to reach the target wins.
4) Modify the game so all teammates must touch the ball to score, or play toward a shared target number like 31 passes.

1) Set up a 20-step square grid using cones and select one chaser through rock-paper-scissors.
2) Passers keep possession by kicking the soccer ball around the grid while the chaser attempts to win it.
3) Passers win by completing 20 consecutive passes, while the chaser wins by stealing the ball or forcing it out of bounds.
4) Place the chaser in the middle of a circle to reward cross-passes, or increase the number of chasers to two.

1) Set score zones on a badminton court (corners 3 pts, small boxes 2 pts, large boxes 1 pt) and form teams of three players.
2) Players stand at the service line and stroke three shuttlecocks each toward the designated target area across the net.
3) Teams score points where shuttlecocks land, receiving zero points for lines or outs, and add all three players' scores to determine the winner.
4) Adjust shooting distance markers for different skill levels or add a defensive goalkeeper with a racket for a shootout variation.
스내그 골프 롤링 타깃 맞히기 스테이션 활동
스내그 골프 롤러 6개, 롤링 타깃 3세트, 불스아이 타깃 3개, 스내그 골프공 20개
SNAG Golf Rolling Target Station Accuracy Challenge

1) Set up Bulls Eye and roller targets in the gym and divide students into station groups.
2) Use the SNAG roller club to roll or chip the ball toward the designated target area.
3) Score points when the ball sticks to the velcro target face and record group totals.
4) Vary the challenge by introducing bounce shots or adjusting the distance to the target.
6 SNAG roller clubs, 3 rolling targets, 3 Bullseye targets, 20 SNAG golf balls
초등 배드민턴 동아리 하프스매시 및 단식 경기
Elementary Badminton Club Half Smash and Singles Match

1) Stand face-to-face across the net and grip the racket using standard handshake form.
2) Deliver a diagonal serve and exchange high clears deep into the backcourt.
3) Score points by snapping the wrist on short chance balls to drive a half smash downward.
4) Play a fast-paced 9-point singles challenge to determine the match winner.
4 badminton rackets, 10 shuttlecocks, 1 badminton net set
Cicada Tag along the Tree Lines

1) Designate gymnasium court lines as tree branches and pick one tagger via rock-paper-scissors to hold a foam balloon bat.
2) All players must only step on and walk along the gym lines to evade the tagger.
3) Stepping off a line or getting tagged causes an out, requiring a lap around the perimeter or taking over the balloon bat.
4) Add variations by allowing the tagger to jump between lines or progressively increasing movement speed from walking to running.
Frog Hop Crossing the Lily Pond

1) Arrange spot markers in an S-shaped path and divide students into two teams lined up at opposite ends.
2) On start, the lead runners jump two-footed from spot to spot moving toward each other.
3) When they meet, they play rock-paper-scissors; the loser returns to their team line as the next teammate launches, while the winner keeps jumping forward.
4) Reaching the opponent's base marker scores 1 point, and the team with the most points after 3 minutes wins.
15 spot markers, team pinnies, 1 flip scoreboard
스쿠터보드 2대, 구명조끼 2벌, 훌라후프 2개, 콩주머니 10개, 페트병 2개, 긴 줄 4개, 매트 4장, 타깃 표적판 2개

1) Set up a 4-station circuit (back-float glide, life jacket donning, life ring rescue, rope-tied bottle throw).
2) Runners lie on scooter boards to pull themselves forward, then put on and take off a life jacket correctly at station two.
3) Throw a hula-hoop life ring to collect and rescue 5 beanbags representing swimmers in distress.
4) Tie a rescue rope to a water bottle, toss it onto the circular target board, and return to tag the next runner after peer verification.
2 scooter boards, 2 life vests, 2 hula hoops, 10 beanbags, 2 plastic bottles, 4 long ropes, 4 mats, 2 target boards
Finding Neighboring Houses with Basic Rhythm Steps

1) Place spot markers equal to the number of students spread across the gym, having each child stand on their initial home marker.
2) Practice 4 fundamental movement steps (walk, run, jump, skip) while visiting and memorizing houses 2, 3, and 4 in order.
3) Listen for teacher prompts such as 'Go to House 3 skipping!' and navigate to the assigned spot marker using the designated step.
4) Progress by introducing hopping, galloping, side steps, or calling out marker colors matched to specific movements.

1) Place spot markers equal to the total player count in a wide layout and appoint one tagger wearing a team pinny in the center.
2) The tagger slowly walks like a turtle toward the only empty marker while other students walk to fill empty spots.
3) Whenever a student vacates a spot, nearby peers continuously step in to fill the newly opened gap before the turtle arrives.
4) If the tagger successfully claims an open spot, they pass the pinny to a new volunteer, or add a second tagger for greater difficulty.
원형 대형으로 즐기는 강강술래 전통 춤 놀이

1) All students hold hands facing inwards in a large circle to prepare.
2) Move counterclockwise walking and jogging to the rhythm while responding to the lead singer's call.
3) Perform variations such as the Namsaengi tortoise mimic dance in pairs and the deokseok rolling-unrolling spiral movement following the leader.
4) Expand the activity by incorporating regional step styles or group formation shifts.
모둠 협동 리본 리듬 표현 창작 및 발표 활동
Cooperative Ribbon Rhythm Expression and Performance

1) Groups practice the eight basic ribbon movements in assigned sequential order.
2) Choose an upbeat piece of music and analyze its tempo and rhythm sections.
3) Choreograph wave, circle, and shaking ribbon patterns matching each musical phrase.
4) Perform the completed routine in front of peers and exchange positive feedback.
One rhythmic gymnastics ribbon per student
음악 리듬 감각 익히기 스팟 마커 자리 찾기 놀이
Rhythm Movement and Spot Marker Station Game

1) Each student drops a spot marker on the floor to mark position 1.
2) Move freely across the gym walking or jogging in sync with the tempo and dynamics of background music.
3) Freeze on signal and place markers down to establish and memorize stations 2 and 3 sequentially.
4) Transition rhythmically to designated target stations called out by the teacher.
꽃과 봉오리 협동 구출 술래잡기 놀이

1) Set up boundaries with cones and designate 1 to 3 taggers wearing scrimmage vests.
2) Runners evade taggers, calling out "Flower" and raising hands overhead like a closed bud to become safe before being tagged.
3) Frozen players are rescued only when two free classmates simultaneously lower each arm shouting "Bud".
4) Add variations by modifying the frozen flower pose or restricting movement methods to hopping or skipping.
실용 무용 케이팝 포인트 안무 바꾸기

1) Choose a K-pop song from the given tracks and identify the recurring signature point dance moves.
2) Design an original hand and arm movement using familiar daily gestures or finger hearts.
3) Combine upper-body gestures with footwork, connecting introductory and ending poses to complete the routine.
4) Practice in small groups to vary formations and perform the newly created dance in front of classmates.
사막에서 물을 찾은 기쁨! 이스라엘 민속춤 마임
Mayim Mayim: Israeli Folk Dance Celebration

1) Stand alternately holding hands in a circle and bounce knees lightly to the rhythm of the music.
2) Perform grapevine steps crossing the left foot front and back while moving clockwise.
3) Move toward the center lifting arms to tap feet, then walk backward to reopen the circle.
4) Walk four steps clockwise, then jump to tap feet and clap hands with neighbors, repeating the sequence.

1) Pair up with a partner, taking one soft foam ball per pair, and scatter around the activity area.
2) On the teacher's first whistle, practice tossing and catching the soft foam ball back and forth.
3) On the next whistle, the student with the ball becomes the squirrel, does 3 jumping jacks, and walks to tag their partner (acorn).
4) When two whistles blow, stop chasing and resume tossing, or vary the chase locomotion with skipping or galloping.
Lyrical Dance Making: Creating Movements from Song Lyrics

1) Select a moderately paced song with meaningful lyrics and identify key words or sentences.
2) Brainstorm upper-body and hand gestures that directly express the imagery of chosen lyrical phrases.
3) Refine the gesture to match the musical rhythm, amplify movement size, and combine it with lower-body footwork.
4) Write down movement notes next to the lyric sheet and progressively expand choreography across the entire verse.
표현 요소를 익히는 거울 놀이와 움직임 탐색
Mirror Mirror Movement: Exploring Expressive Elements

1) Spread out across the gym and express movement effort qualities (slow, fast, heavy, light) based on verbal cues.
2) Move through general space incorporating spatial elements like high/low levels and straight/zigzag/curved paths.
3) Form pairs or small groups of three, play rock-paper-scissors to assign a leader, who initiates creative body movements.
4) The partners mirror the leader's bodily motions simultaneously, alternating leader roles to music cues.

1) One student is chosen as the tagger, and all other students balance a saucer cone on their heads within the boundaries.
2) The tagger walks to chase players and gently taps off the cones balanced on their heads.
3) Players whose cones fall must freeze in place, but teammates can revive them by picking up the cone and placing it back on their head.
4) The game can be modified into a team battle knocking off opponent cones or by balancing spots on open hands instead.

1) Teams line up with two cones marking turning points per team and a central collection basket placed in the middle.
2) The first runner balances a beanbag on their head, walks around both turning points, and passes it to the end of the line shouting "Dandelion!".
3) The beanbag is passed to the front runner for the next turn, and the final runner finishes by dropping the beanbag into the central basket.
4) The difficulty can be modified by balancing beanbags on the shoulders or feet, or hopping with beanbags squeezed between the knees.
나는야 눈싸움 왕 훌라후프 표적 던지기

1) Teams wear scrimmage vests, line up behind the starting basket, and place a hula hoop on the floor 2 meters ahead.
2) On the start signal, the first player picks up a beanbag, aims, throws it into the hoop, and runs to the back of the line.
3) Teammates take turns throwing, and once all beanbags are used, they collect them together; the team with the most beanbags inside the hoop wins.
4) Adjust the throwing distance or replace the hula hoop with mini goalposts, bowling pins, or plastic bottles for variety.
20 beanbags, 4 hula hoops, 4 baskets, scrimmage vests

1) Set up a rectangular court, divide students into two teams, and designate one invincible bodyguard per team who wears a team vest.
2) Once the game starts, bodyguards step forward to block incoming throws while teammates dodge to avoid being hit.
3) Regular players are eliminated upon getting hit, and once all teammates are out, the bodyguard loses invincibility and can be eliminated for the final win.
4) For larger classes or mixed skill levels, increase the number of bodyguards or pair students up into partner dodgeball.
플로어볼 스틱(학생 수만큼), 플로어볼 공 여러 개, 골대 2개, 골키퍼 보호장비 2세트, 팀 조끼

1) Learn the basic stance and grip, then practice short tap dribbling between feet and low push passes along the floor.
2) Set up a triangular stance with the ball and both feet, keeping the blade flush to the ground to practice accurate shooting.
3) Form two teams with goalkeepers and play a regular mini-game where passing and dribbling lead to scoring in the opponent net.
4) Add a penalty shootout challenge where players take five designated attempts to test target-scoring proficiency.
Floorball sticks (one per student), floorball balls, 2 goals, 2 goalkeeper gear sets, team vests
플라잉디스크 여러 개, 점보스택스 컵 세트, 라바콘 여러 개, 디스캐처(또는 물병)

1) Set up target obstacles such as cones, stacking cups, or disc catchers at a safe distance and mark a clear throwing line.
2) Students take turns throwing flying discs toward the targets with 3 practice attempts per person from adjustable distances.
3) Run a team challenge where members alternate throws to hit or land discs into the targets, totaling scores to decide the winner.
4) Vary the activity into disc bowling using water bottles as pins, or set a 1-minute time limit for a rapid target-shooting contest.
Flying discs, jumbo stacking cup sets, cones, disc golf catchers (or plastic bottles)
팀 조끼(팀 구분용), 바닥 마킹 테이프

1) Prepare a compact 5m space and have students sit facing each other in small teams or 1-on-1 pairs.
2) Play simple turn-based hand games such as Zero Game, Rock-Paper-Scissors, or Muk-Jji-Ppa.
3) The losing student or team performs a designated number of burpees (e.g., 3, 6, or 10 reps) as a fitness challenge.
4) Transform the activity into a burpee quiz battle where players jump to O/X answer zones and wrong answers trigger 3–5 burpees.
배구공 1개, 낮은 배구 네트(또는 바닥 표시용 라인 테이프/콘)

1) Set up a low net or boundary box on the court and divide students into teams of 2 to 3 players.
2) The server serves with one hand, and the receiving team must catch (C) the ball after exactly one bounce.
3) Teammates pass (P) the ball in the air without letting it bounce, ensuring every member touches the ball before spiking (S) it over.
4) Teams score when the ball lands in the opponent's court or on opponent faults, and bonus points can be awarded for jump spikes or overhand serves.
1 volleyball, 1 low net (or floor marking tape/cones)
노래에 맞춰 뛰는 전통 고무줄 놀이

1) Two players stretch an elastic band around their ankles while jumpers line up to take turns.
2) Jumpers perform an 8-beat stepping pattern in sync with the song, hopping over and across the band.
3) Players clear the stage by finishing the pattern without tripping, while missing a step or rhythm switches their role with a holder.
4) Increase the difficulty by raising the band height to shins and waist, or by forming a triangle with three holders.
바닥 라인 테이프(또는 출발선 표시용 분필)
Fox, Fox, What Are You Doing?

1) Mark a starting line and place the tagger (fox) 15-20 steps away facing backwards.
2) Runners slowly approach the fox while chanting the traditional call-and-response song together.
3) If the fox responds "I'm dead" and turns around, runners must freeze, and anyone caught moving becomes the new fox.
4) If the fox shouts "I'm alive!", runners sprint back to the safe zone behind the starting line before the fox tags them.
Floor tape (or chalk for marking lines)
목표 상자에 넣는 배구 퐁당 챌린지

1) One challenger faces a line of 3 to 4 runners, with a target ball box placed at the end of the line.
2) Runner 1 throws or passes the ball to the challenger, who bumps or sets it forward to Runner 2, who then returns it to the challenger.
3) The challenger continues the zigzag passing rally back and forth down the line with each runner without dropping the ball.
4) The challenger scores by setting the final returned ball directly into the target box, with variations allowing one bounce or requiring consecutive forearm passes.
배드민턴 라켓 4~6개, 셔틀콕 다수, 팀 조끼

1) Players line up along the service line of a regulation badminton court holding rackets and shuttlecocks.
2) On signal, all players stroke their shuttlecocks simultaneously; the longest valid shot within the court boundary scores top points.
3) The top hitter is set aside per round while remaining players compete again to accumulate total ranking points.
4) Transition into 3v3 team relays or a timed 5-stage trick lifting sequence passing the racket around the waist or legs.
배드민턴 라켓 4개, 셔틀콕 2개, 라바콘 2개, 간이 네트, 팀 조끼

1) Pairs face each other in a high-ceiling gymnasium with rackets and shuttlecocks separated by a net or center line.
2) Avoid smashing and gently send the shuttlecock to your partner's chest level to maintain the longest possible rally.
3) Perform cooperative challenges between hits, such as a full body spin, ground-touch squat, or non-dominant hand hitting.
4) Expand to a 2v2 format where the player who hits rotates behind their teammate to sustain continuous team rallies.
4 badminton rackets, 2 shuttlecocks, 2 cones, portable net, team pinnies
리듬 온! 지시 앤 포토 창작댄스

1) Form groups of three or more, select one student as the director (leader), and set up an 8-count background rhythm.
2) Compose an 8-count command dance where the leader gestures directional pushes, squats, and stomps while members react accordingly.
3) Connect a photo dance where dancers freeze every two beats representing glass-wall traps, vacation photos, or sports actions.
4) Conclude the routine with a cooperative structure dance holding hands and balancing together to form a flower or heart shape.

1) Teams of 3 to 6 line up in single file at the start line with one basketball and a turning cone set at the finish.
2) On the starting signal, players pass the ball backward using designated methods such as between-the-legs rolling, overhead passing, or bounce passing.
3) The front player passes the ball and immediately sprints to the back of the line to advance the team toward the goal cone.
4) As an advanced variation, have players face a backboard and take turns keeping the basketball rebounding off the board continuously.

1) Two players divide 20 marbles equally (10 each) and set up a target circle or triangle layout on a floor mat.
2) From three paces behind the throw line, players roll a marble closest to the target circle or knock cluster marbles out of the triangle.
3) Players collect any marbles knocked out of the boundary, or flick their marble to hit the opponent's marble directly to win it.
4) Increase challenge by setting up paper plate targets or throwing with variations like eyes closed or standing on one foot.

1) Set up a course using cones, hazard mats for swamps/lakes, and two target disc catchers across the playing area.
2) Form teams of 2 to 3 players and take turns throwing the flying disc from the tee line toward the target.
3) Place a cone where the disc lands for the next teammate's lie, competing to hole out in the disc catcher first.
4) Apply fun hazard penalties such as throwing from a deep squat when landing in the swamp or re-throwing if landing in water.
4 flying discs, 2 disc catchers, 2 cones, 2 mats

1) Divide the court into Goal Third, Center Third, and Defense Third, positioning 3+ players per team wearing vests in designated zones.
2) The disc carrier cannot run but may pivot, and passes must progress zone by zone without skipping two zones at once.
3) Teams score 1 point by landing the disc in the opponent's catcher or hitting it; incomplete passes or defensive deflections turnover possession.
4) Vary game dynamics by narrowing zone sizes, allowing teammates to act as goals, or reshaping the field into an oval arena.
2 flying discs, 2 disc catchers, 12 team vests
돌 던지고 균형 잡아 구역 따는 사방치기
놀이 바닥판 1개, 망(돌멩이/지우개) 2개, 구역 표시용 말 4개

1) Set up a 1-to-8 court with a heaven zone on the ground and prepare a stone marker for each player.
2) Throw the marker starting from square 1, jump through the numbered squares using one foot or two feet avoiding the marker square, and retrieve the marker on the way back.
3) After completing all 8 stages, stand in the heaven zone, toss the marker backward, and claim the landing spot as your territory.
4) The territory owner can rest with both feet inside, while opponents must leap completely over it.
1 hopscotch mat, 2 stone markers, 4 territory tokens
동작 뽑고 대형 바꾸는 생각대로 라인댄스

1) Learn basic line dance steps including step, touch, cross, kick, and pivot turn, and thoroughly warm up wrist and ankle joints.
2) Draw mission slips containing basic step combinations and collaborate in groups to create four original dance steps.
3) Link the steps in sequence to an 8-beat rhythm track while turning towards four different directions.
4) During the final four beats of the fourth step, transition positions to form creative team shapes like straight lines and V-formations.
신체 접촉 없는 패스 축구 디스크 싸커

1) Teams put on colored vests, line up at opposite end lines, and launch the disc into play upon the referee's signal.
2) The player holding the disc cannot run and may only pivot on one foot, advancing down the court solely through teammate passes into open spaces.
3) A team scores 1 point by throwing the disc directly into the opponent's soccer goal; dropped passes or interceptions immediately switch possession.
4) Defenders must maintain a 1-meter cushion without physical contact, and games can be modified to target basketball hoops using hammer throws.
1 flying disc, 10 team vests, 2 mini soccer goals

1) Draw a circle on the ground and play rock-paper-scissors to determine each player's turn order.
2) Players register in order by stepping into the circle on one foot saying "Don" and jumping out landing on both feet saying "Gas."
3) Player 1 chooses to call either "Don-Gas" (step on circle then attack) or "Gas" (attack immediately) to tag an opponent's foot, while subsequent players must copy the same call.
4) A player is eliminated if their foot is tagged or if they step on boundary lines, and advanced rules allow chaining up to three consecutive attacks.
거리 조절 플라잉 디스크 패스 챌린지

1) Pair up students facing each other at an initial distance of about five paces with a safe foam flying disc.
2) Gently push and release the disc forward towards the partner to initiate back-and-forth throwing and catching.
3) Take one step backward upon each successful catch to increase distance, or take one step forward if dropped.
4) As an advanced modification, place a net between players so discs must travel over it, or rotate players in a relay line.
릴레이 배드민턴 앤 코트 로테이션 랠리

1) Form teams of 3 to 6 players on a standard badminton court and set up cones as turnaround markers.
2) In the relay stage, players carry a shuttlecock on their racket while walking, hopping on one foot, or jumping with both feet around the cones.
3) In the rally stage, three players stand on each side of the court, hit the shuttlecock over the net, and rotate to the back of their line to complete team rallies for points.
4) For an advanced variation, have players bounce the shuttlecock repeatedly during the relay, or assign one skilled player against five rotating teammates.

1) Draw a circle 2 to 3 paces wide on the ground and determine the jumping order through rock-paper-scissors.
2) Jump over the circle without touching it on "Heo," take single-step leaps on "Su," "A," and freeze entirely like a scarecrow on "Bi."
3) Once everyone is frozen in position, players take turns stepping past obstacles in original order to safely escape past the finish boundary.
4) Moving after freezing, touching another scarecrow, or stepping on the circle line causes elimination, with variations including single-leg stances.
스피드스택스 전용 컵 12개 2세트, 스태킹 매트 2개, 타이머 2대, 경기용 책상 2개

1) Set up dedicated mats, timers, and cup sets on tables for each team and determine the order of players.
2) On signal, stack and downstack the cups quickly in individual (such as 3-6-3) or doubles format.
3) The team that finishes faster or completes the routine without scratching when stopping the timer wins the point.
4) Modify by rotating match orders or running a 4-person team relay over multiple sets.
2 sets of 12 stacking cups, 2 stacking mats, 2 timers, 2 tables
넷볼 공(또는 4~5호 배구공) 1개, 넷볼 골대 2대, 7개 포지션 팀 조끼 2세트
Elementary School Sports Club Netball Game

1) Put on bibs indicating 7 designated positions (GS, GA, WA, C, WD, GD, GK) and position players in their allowed thirds of the court.
2) Start with a center pass and advance the ball toward the goal circle using pivoting and passing without dribbling.
3) Inside the goal circle, GS and GA take shots or penalty shots into the ring without a backboard to score 1 point per goal.
4) Modify by rotating position bibs each quarter or extending the ball possession limit from 3 to 5 seconds for beginners.
1 netball, 2 netball goal posts, 2 sets of 7-position team bibs
피구공 1개, 팀 조끼 2세트, 경기장 라인 마킹 테이프

1) Position 10-12 players in the infield and 1-2 players in the outfield for each team with team bibs on a divided court.
2) Win the opening possession via a jump ball, then throw at opponents using coordinated passing between infield and outfield.
3) Hit players move to the outfield, and the team with more active infielders remaining when time expires wins the set.
4) Attempt double-out combination throws or regain possession immediately whenever a defender cleanly catches the thrown ball.
1 dodgeball, 2 sets of team bibs, court boundary tape

1) Pair up with one basketball; the offensive player takes a triple-threat stance holding the ball near the chin, while the defender assumes a stance guarding shooting and passing lanes.
2) On signal, the offensive player executes one motion among shoot, pass, or dribble, while the defender simultaneously mirrors a high (shot), middle (pass), or low (dribble) guard.
3) If the defender matches the offensive player's choice, defense succeeds and ball possession switches; otherwise, the offense scores 1 point.
4) The player who reaches 5 points first wins the match, and the losing partner performs a simple penalty before rotating.

1) Set a starting line about 15m away from the sandpit and prepare the takeoff board line and landing pit.
2) On the starting signal, accelerate at top speed through the 15-meter approach run.
3) Take off powerfully from one foot without stepping on or crossing the foul line, lifting the body at about a 30-degree angle.
4) Land softly in the sandpit by bending both knees to absorb impact, measuring distance over 3 trials for the best score.
Takeoff tape line, measuring tape, sand rake
넷볼 공 4개, 넷볼 골대 2개, 포지션 마킹 팀조끼 14벌

1) Put on position bibs (GS, GA, WA, C, WD, GD, GK) and confirm the assigned court areas and backboard-free rings.
2) The offensive team advances by passing zig-zag without dribbling, releasing the ball within 3 seconds.
3) Defenders must stay at least 90cm away from the ball carrier while reading fake moves to intercept passes.
4) Pass the ball to the shooters (GS, GA) inside the goal circle to score; the team with the most points wins.
4 netballs, 2 netball goal posts, 14 position bibs

1) Divide the court into infield and outfield, split players into two teams, and wear team bibs.
2) Pass the ball rapidly between infield and outfield to throw at opposing infielders.
3) Hit players move to the outfield, and the team eliminating all opponents or having more survivors scores the set.
4) Play can be modified by introducing multiple balls or adjusting initial outfield counts.

1) Mark the court with infield and outfield lines and set up more than 10 players on each team.
2) Distract opponents with jump passes and outfield long balls, then target their lower body.
3) Eliminate opponents by hitting them with the ball, while catching rebounds maintains possession.
4) Modify the match by setting a 3 to 5-minute timer or restricting throws to specific outfield areas.
플로어볼 스틱 12개, 플로어볼 공 1개, 플로어볼 골대 2개, 팀 조끼 12벌

1) Set up goals at each end, assign field players and goalies, and equip sticks and team bibs.
2) Dribble and pass the floorball using the stick blade while advancing toward the opposing goal.
3) Score 1 point by shooting the floorball into the opponent's goal net.
4) Modify rules by restricting stick swings below knee level or using mini goals without goalies.
12 floorball sticks, 1 floorball, 2 floorball goals, 12 team bibs

1) Mark boundaries for infield and outfield, dividing teams into designated infielders and outfielders.
2) Shift possession rapidly between central infield and sideline outfielders to open up throwing angles.
3) Eliminate opponent infielders by hitting them, with the team preserving more players winning the set.
4) Apply modifications such as a 5-second possession limit or simplified interference rules.
스텝 앤 캐치 배구 기본기 서킷 트레이닝
Volleyball Circuit Training for Fundamental Skills

1) Set up cone zones on both sides of the gymnasium and divide students into four groups alternating between drill players and ball retrievers.
2) On the whistle, dash forward to the cone, plant the feet, and use leg power to bump the tossed ball with an underhand pass.
3) Rotate through side-step defense, two-step setting, attack approaches, and floating serves to master each basic technique.
4) Track scores by counting consecutive successful pass connections or accurate serves landing inside the designated boundary zones.
스피드스태킹 컵 세트(12개) 2세트, 스택스 매트 및 타이머 2세트
Elephant Spin Speed Stacking Relay Challenge

1) Set up two sets of 12 stacking cups and timer mats on desks, marking a spin line a few meters behind.
2) Tap the timer mat with both palms to start, run back to the line, and spin 5 times in an elephant-trunk posture.
3) Rush back to the table and accurately complete the designated stack (3-3-3 or 3-6-3) by building up and down with alternating hands.
4) Stack all cups back down, hit the stop pad with both palms, and compare total times to declare the winner.
2 sets of 12 Speed Stacks cups, 2 StackMats with timers
ePAPS 타바타 하체 근력 단련 서킷
ePAPS High-Intensity Lower Body Strength Workout

가을 테마 이동운동 듣고 멈추기 놀이
Fall Locomotor Listen & Move Freeze Game

1) Spread out safely across the room and listen closely to the audio cues.
2) Perform the designated autumn-themed locomotor movements (turkey walk, crow flight, bear crawl, squirrel jog) along with the music.
3) Instantly freeze like a statue and hold balance when the whistle blows and 'Freeze' appears.
4) Move to round two at a faster pace, sharpening listening skills and body control until the activity ends.
스팟 마커 토스 앤 캐치 단계별 챌린지

1) Each student stands or sits on their designated home spot marker with a soft ball.
2) Start sitting on the floor, tossing the ball gently with two hands or one hand and catching with two hands.
3) Advance through progressive postures: kneeling, standing, one-foot balance, and tossing-clapping before catching.
4) Conclude by inventing and practicing a unique toss-and-catch challenge while maintaining control on the spot.
1 foam ball and 1 spot marker per student
토끼 그리기와 무브 타바타 브레인 브레이크
Draw and Move: Bunny Rabbit Brain Break

1) Prepare paper and a pencil, then look at the screen to choose a preferred bunny feature (face, ears, eyes, nose, mouth, whiskers).
2) Perform the assigned exercise (jog in place, star jumps, high knees, cat/cow yoga pose) for 30 seconds.
3) Pick up the pencil after the exercise interval and draw the selected bunny feature on paper within 30 seconds.
4) Use the final 30 seconds to color and complete the bunny drawing, then share the artwork with classmates.
1 sheet of paper and 1 pencil per student

1) Stand in place facing the screen ensuring enough personal movement space.
2) Choose one preferred movement among the three choices shown on screen and perform it to the music for 30 seconds.
3) Catch your breath and reset during the 10-second rest break between rounds.
4) Adapt your workout each round by alternating between challenging exercises and fun Fortnite dance moves to finish all sets.
Shapes & Stacks Cup Stacking Fitness Challenge

1) Each student prepares 12 stacking cups in a single stack on a desk or floor.
2) When a shape appears on the screen, arrange all cups to replicate the image within the 1-minute timer.
3) If you finish the cup shape early, immediately perform the designated fitness exercise shown on screen until time expires.
4) Use the 10-second reset interval to re-stack your cups into a single column before starting the next challenge.

1) Set up boundary cones along the gym perimeter and assign students into pairs where one plays and the other rests at a cone.
2) Active players balance a poly spot flat on their upturned palm like a pizza waiter and navigate the court.
3) Players attempt to flip the poly spots off their opponents' hands while keeping their own pizza balanced inside the lines.
4) If a player's pizza drops or they step out of bounds, they raise their hand overhead, walk safely to their partner at the cone, and switch roles.
Jump Rope This or That Fitness Interval

1) Each student holds a jump rope and spaces out safely so their rope will not tangle with classmates.
2) In each round, look at the screen and choose one of the two featured jump rope skills.
3) Jump continuously using your chosen technique for the entire 30-second work interval.
4) Rest and recover your breathing during the 20-second break between rounds before tackling the next pair of skills.
농구 홈스팟 볼핸들링 & 드리블 인터벌 드릴
농구공 학급 인원수(약 25개), 원마커 학급 인원수(약 25개)
Basketball Ball Handling & Dribbling Drill Follow-Along

1) Each student stands on an assigned floor poly spot holding one basketball.
2) Follow the screen prompts to perform foundational ball-handling tasks including ball slaps, finger taps, and waist wraps.
3) Practice on-the-spot basketball techniques such as pivoting, one-handed dribbles, crossovers, and between-the-legs dribbles according to the countdown timer.
4) In the final round, combine the practiced moves to create and demonstrate your own creative dribbling sequence.
Basketballs for each student (approx. 25), poly spots (approx. 25)

1) Each student holds one or two foam noodle bits and scatters across the activity area.
2) On the start signal, players move around and attempt to pop their noodle bit off another player's back.
3) Popping a noodle bit off an opponent's back scores 1 point, and catching it in the air after the pop awards a bonus point for a total of 2 points.
4) To increase difficulty, players can hold two noodle bits at once or compete to achieve the highest score within a set time limit.

1) Set up a bowling pin in the center and position two teams behind the baseline with basketballs.
2) On the signal, players take turns rolling the basketball along the floor to knock down the pin first.
3) The team that hits the pin races to the basket to shoot layups for points, while the other team performs ten chest passes under their own basket.
4) When the passing team completes ten passes, shooting stops and players reset the pin for the next round.

1) Students sit on the floor in a circle, holding a half foam noodle horizontally with both hands.
2) Follow the teacher's cues or music rhythm to bend the noodle into circles and curls to engage upper-body muscles.
3) Clap the noodles together overhead, in front of the chest, and downward, then twist them into an S-shape like pedaling a bicycle.
4) Progress into overhead press combos and single-arm curls while gradually increasing the movement speed.

1) All students stand evenly spaced around the parachute, holding the outer edges with both hands.
2) On the leader's signal, everyone lifts the parachute high overhead together to create a large floating dome.
3) When the leader calls out a specific shirt color, students wearing that color walk underneath to the opposite side.
4) For variation, players can take a giant step inside to pitch a tent or add tossing numbers on top for a math challenge.

1) Students scatter across the playing area, and half of the players hold a 7-inch coated foam ball of different colors.
2) The ball carrier quickly completes three passes to a partner who signals with open hands.
3) After completing three passes, the player relinquishes the ball, becomes an open receiver, and seeks out a different colored ball.
4) Add variations such as requiring all three throws to be bounce passes or prohibiting receiving the same color consecutively.

1) Students pair up facing each other behind a line of numbered cones spaced across the gym.
2) One partner tosses the ball underhand, and the opposite partner volleys it back out of the air using the inside of the foot into their hands.
3) After completing a successful volley with both right and left feet, partners swap positions and advance to the next numbered cone.
4) Teams race to cycle through cones 1 through 6, then conclude with a continuous zigzag dribbling challenge through the course.
녹 하키 전용 보드 1개, 미니 하키 스틱 2개, 퍽 1개

1) Two players take positions at opposite ends of the Nok Hockey board holding a mini stick.
2) When the puck is on your half, strike it toward the opposing goal in a single hit without stick-handling.
3) Score a point by shooting directly or banking the puck off the side cushions into the goal.
4) Switch to a two-on-two tag team format where partners alternate taking shots.
1 Nok Hockey board, 2 mini sticks, 1 puck

1) Each student stands beside their desk holding juggling scarves in both hands.
2) Move your arms in large circles and trace alphabet letters in the air as instructed.
3) Solve calling math problems while tossing and catching the scarf to match the rhythm.
4) Progress into quick-reaction drills by dropping and snatching scarves out of the air.
풀누들 타깃 투척 및 누들 하키
Pool Noodle Target Throw and Hockey

1) Students each hold a pool noodle and space out facing the gym wall.
2) Throw the noodle overhand toward the wall target using a javelin throwing technique.
3) Pair up to roll, toss, and balance a soft foam ball together along the noodles.
4) Transition into team noodle hockey by holding both ends of the noodle to strike the ball into the wall.
츄크볼 전용 프레임(바운더) 2대, 츄크볼(핸드볼 크기 공) 1개, 라바콘 12개

1) Set up a rebound frame and a semicircular forbidden zone at each end line, and divide the class into two teams.
2) A player holding the ball may not take more than 3 steps, and the team must connect passes within 3 passes to shoot at a frame.
3) If the ball rebounds off the frame and lands on the court floor outside the forbidden zone, the team scores; if a defender catches it directly, no point is scored.
4) Players may not intercept an opponent's pass or shot directly, and the two-way rule applies, so either frame may be attacked.
2 tchoukball rebound frames, 1 tchoukball (or soft handball), 12 cones
이클립스볼 전용 라켓 12개, 이클립스볼(대형 깃털 폼볼) 2개, 네트 또는 라바콘

1) Divide players across the center line or net, each holding an eclipse ball paddle with a firm wrist.
2) Serve the ball over the net after letting it bounce once on the floor.
3) Set up passes among teammates allowing one bounce between hits before returning it over.
4) Play multi-player games where consecutive hits by the same player are prohibited.
12 Eclipse Ball rackets, 2 Eclipse balls, 1 badminton net (or cones)
소방대 물통 전달 릴레이 (빈백 버킷 브리게이드)

1) Teams line up in a single file between the water source disc and the fire target disc.
2) The front player picks up a bean bag and passes it over the left shoulder to the teammate behind.
3) After passing, the runner sprints along the side to the very back of the line to continue receiving.
4) The first team to transfer all bean bags to the final target disc to extinguish the fire wins.
발로 콘 잡기 스쿠터 릴레이 (콘 그랩)

1) Students pair up with one sitting on the scooter board and the other standing behind to push.
2) On the start signal, the pusher navigates the scooter forward toward a target cone.
3) The rider must grasp and lift the cone using only their feet without touching it with hands.
4) The team races back to the start holding the cone and tags the next pair to finish first.
초등 기초 피클볼 랠리 (더블 바운스 챌린지)
피클볼 라켓 4개, 피클볼 공 2개, 미니 네트 세트 1개

1) Players set up in doubles on opposite sides of a low portable net holding pickleball paddles.
2) The server executes an underhand serve striking the ball below the navel into the diagonal court.
3) Both the serve and the return must bounce once on each side before any volley is allowed (Double Bounce Rule).
4) Players continue the rally with flat paddle strikes, scoring points when opponents commit a fault.
4 pickleball paddles, 2 pickleballs, 1 mini net set
공중 9칸 배구 게임 (나인 스퀘어 인 디 에어)
9 Square in the Air Volleyball Game

1) Nine players enter the elevated 3x3 grid structure, each occupying a designated square numbered 1 to 9.
2) The player in the center square (#9/King) serves the ball up and over the top frame into another square.
3) Players use volleyball overhead sets or hits to keep the ball airborne and direct it out of their square on one touch.
4) When a player misses or hits out of bounds, they rotate to square 1 while others move up toward the center.

1) Each student takes up to three scarves and holds the center pinch to form a ghost shape.
2) With one scarf, lift gently upward and catch on the descent using a downward palm claw catch.
3) With two scarves, practice the criss-cross X-pattern calling out 'throw, throw, catch, catch' alternately.
4) Progress to three scarves, starting with the hand holding two, maintaining a rhythm with only one scarf in the air at a time.

1) Mark a 15m or 20m running course across the gym and pair up students into two-person teams.
2) The first runner jogs across to the opposite line in sync with the audio beeps, tags their partner's hand, and switches roles.
3) Partners alternate laps to manage fatigue, with stronger runners allowed to take consecutive turns to give their partner a rest.
4) The test ends when the team fails to cross the line before the beep twice, recording the total successful laps completed.

1) Fold and create three paper airplanes and place a laundry basket or bucket 5 to 10 feet away from the throwing line.
2) Start a 1-minute timer and throw the three paper airplanes one by one from behind the throwing line toward the basket.
3) Score 1 point if an airplane hits the outside of the basket and 2 points if it lands inside, quickly retrieving and re-throwing within the time limit.
4) Adjust the challenge by moving the basket further away or using a smaller target bucket to increase difficulty.
3 paper airplanes, 1 laundry basket (or bucket), timer
미니 농구공 여러 개, 농구 골대

1) Students line up at an appropriate distance around the basketball hoops with small arcade basketballs.
2) Review and practice the four core shooting cues of B.E.E.F. (Balance, Eyes, Elbow, Follow-through).
3) Follow the leader's demonstrated form and shoot toward the back of the basketball rim.
4) As a modification for more power, students bend their knees and jump during the shot instead of standing still.
매트 10장 이상, 미니 트램펄린 1개, 뜀틀 블록 매트 세트, 점프 박스 2~4개, 평균대 2개, 콩주머니 여러 개, 암벽장 및 로프, 번호 표시 콘 8개

1) Set up eight stations across the gym including traveling mat, vault, rock wall, rope swing, balance, jump boxes, balance beam, and partner balance.
2) Divide students into small groups at each numbered station and review the challenge task cards.
3) Practice each skill while music plays, and rotate along the gym lines to the next numbered station when music stops.
4) Modify difficulty by adjusting vault mat height, jumping tricks, or balancing with a bean bag on the head based on grade level.
10+ gymnastics mats, 1 mini trampoline, stacking vault mats, 2-4 jump boxes, 2 balance beams, bean bags, climbing wall, swing ropes, 8 numbered cones
앉아 윗몸 앞으로 굽히기(좌전굴) 유연성 측정
좌전굴 측정기 1대, 신장 체중계 1대, 대기용 벤치 의자

1) Students take off their shoes and line up in orderly fashion behind the sit and reach box.
2) Sit with one leg straight against the box, the other foot flat next to the knee, and fingertips aligned together.
3) Reach forward along the measuring scale as far as possible and hold the stretch for three seconds while the teacher records the score.
4) Switch legs to complete the second trial, then move over to the scale and stadiometer for private height and weight recording.
1 sit and reach box, 1 scale and stadiometer, waiting bench

1) Divide the gym into two courts, place a mat trashcan in each backcourt, and designate one student per team as Oscar inside the trashcan.
2) Scatter foam balls (trash) across the playing area and have students pick up only one ball at a time.
3) Players throw balls into the opposing team's mat using overhand or underhand throws, while Oscar continuously tosses balls out of the can.
4) If a player crosses the center line, they step aside to recite the ABCs before returning, and the team with the least trash in their can wins.

1) Select two taggers holding pool noodles while other students scatter across the open gym space.
2) When music plays, taggers chase runners and tag them gently with their noodles to freeze them.
3) Tagged runners, runners stepping out of bounds, or those falling must stay in place doing a fist pump dance without being unfrozen.
4) The round continues until the music stops, after which new taggers are chosen to begin a new round.

1) Assign one player to each of four marked squares (1-4) and have waiting students line up behind square one.
2) The server in square 4 bounces the ball once behind the service line and strikes it underhand into another player's square.
3) Players must allow the ball to bounce once before striking it into another square; hitting inside lines, double bounces, or hitting out results in an out.
4) The eliminated player moves to the end of the waiting line, players advance up a square number toward square 4, and the next challenger enters square 1.
썬더스틱(긴 줄과 공이 달린 막대) 1개, 훌라후프 5개

1) The turner stands at the center with a thunderstick while students form a circle or stand along court boundary lines.
2) The turner sweeps the thunderstick rope along the floor in a low circle around their feet.
3) Students jump over the incoming rope with timing; anyone whose foot gets struck by the rope is temporarily out.
4) Eliminated students move to an outside station to hula hoop or jog until a final winner remains to reset the game.
1 thunderstick (stick with cord and ball), 5 hula hoops

1) Position two rope turners while students line up single file facing the entry side of the long jump rope.
2) Turners rotate the rope outward from the runners, and students continuously enter the rope the moment the runner ahead leaps.
3) Each student performs exactly one jump and exits smoothly; touching the rope or letting the rope complete an empty turn results in elimination.
4) Eliminated students move to a secondary practice rope to keep active, while top finalists from multiple heats advance to a championship round.

1) Each student spreads out across the gymnasium with one soccer ball ready to dribble.
2) When designated bumpers approach playing light defense, students shield and protect the ball with their body.
3) If a student's ball is bumped out of bounds, they perform 5 push-ups before returning to play.
4) Bumpers pass the role to a quiet hand-raising student to rotate defenders while keeping defense intensity moderate.
Modified Pacer Test for Young Learners

1) Students line up spread out along the gym sideline and observe teacher demonstration laps.
2) On the starting signal, students run straight and slow across the modified short distance before the beep.
3) As test levels increase in speed, students keep pacing; making two consecutive mistakes ends their test.
4) Finished students sit down immediately to cheer silently for peers aiming for 25 to 30 total laps.

1) Adjust the jump rope length by stepping on its center so handles reach armpit height.
2) The teacher stands behind the student and guides their hands to make a big overhead circular turning motion.
3) The student waits for the rope to hit the floor in front of their feet before jumping over it.
4) Once single jumps are mastered, progress to backwards jumping and consecutive jumps of two to five reps.

1) Spread out into open space with safe personal boundaries across the room.
2) Perform four rounds of the 4-count chicken dance consisting of beaks, wings, tail feathers, and claps.
3) During the musical movement break, travel around the open area performing locomotor skills like skipping, sliding, and galloping.
4) Progress by having students square dance with partners or use ribbons and scarves during movement breaks.

1) Scatter a deck of 60 silly task cards face down inside the center circle of the gym.
2) On the start signal, students run in, grab one card, and complete the movement or social interaction challenge with peers.
3) Once completed, hand the card face up to the teacher and immediately grab another card to beat the target time.
4) When the central pile is empty, students without cards actively seek out and assist classmates still finishing tasks.
스텝 앤 푸시 농구 패스 기초 연습
Step and Push Basketball Passing Drills

1) For chest passes, stand 2 steps from a wall; for bounce passes, stand back-to-back with a partner, take 2 steps apart, and face each other.
2) Push the chest pass straight forward from chest level, and push the bounce pass toward the floor about three-quarters of the way to your partner.
3) Extend both arms with thumbs pointing down upon release, and catch incoming balls firmly using both hands.
4) Begin with individual chest passes against the gym wall, then transition into cooperative partner bounce passing practice.
초등 운동회 종목 순환 스테이션 활동
풀누들 12개, 긴줄 4개, 훌라후프 4개, 스태킹컵 4세트, 점핑 자루 4개, 라바콘 8개, 플라잉디스크 8개

1) Set up 18 diverse activity stations across the gym and field, including javelin throw, noodle tower, cup stack relay, and sack race.
2) Divide the class into squads to rotate through stations every 6 minutes upon hearing the air horn signal.
3) Teams score by throwing the farthest, building the tallest self-standing tower, or finishing relay races fastest.
4) Practice game rules with early grades first, then progress to competitive team challenges and championship throw-offs.
12 pool noodles, 4 jump ropes, 4 hula hoops, 4 cup stacking sets, 4 racing sacks, 8 cones, 8 flying discs

1) Pair students up in groups of two or three facing each other in front of a basketball hoop.
2) Both players simultaneously dribble 5 times (or slap the ball 5 times for early grades), then tap their balls together.
3) Immediately following the ball tap, both players sprint to shoot, continuing until someone successfully makes a basket.
4) The first player to score earns a point and resets to the starting mark; the first to reach 3 points wins the match.
Partner Jump Rope Tricks: Face to Face & Side by Side

1) Pair students up with one longer jump rope designated for two jumpers.
2) In 'Face to Face', one partner turns the rope while both jump together facing each other, or the second runner enters mid-turn.
3) In 'Side by Side', each partner holds one handle with their outside hand and coordinates a simultaneous swing and jump.
4) Progress from basic jumps to advanced challenges such as spinning, touching the floor, or jumping in and out of the turning rope.
빙고 학습지 학생당 1장, 마커 학생당 1개, 라바콘 1개

1) Students receive a bingo sheet and marker, then gather in the central square.
2) When music plays, ask a classmate about an adventure activity on the card (one question per person).
3) If they answer yes, have them initial the square, then run to tag the cone and jog one lap before asking another person.
4) Each classmate can sign only once, and players aim to complete 4 or 6 boxes in a row before time runs out.
Bingo sheet per student, marker per student, 1 cone
이것 아니면 저것? 균형 잡기 챌린지
개인용 매트 학급 인원수만큼, 스크린(TV 화면) 1대

1) Students sit on their mats in a pike position and view two balance options shown on screen.
2) On signal, try both balance poses within 30 seconds while engaging core muscles.
3) Hold each balance like a statue for at least 5 seconds to feel the required strength, flexibility, and stability.
4) Progress from basic balances to smaller bases of support and inverted poses, voting and discussing which was more challenging.
Gym mat per student, 1 display screen

1) Set up nine hula hoops in a 3x3 grid and place team cones with three colored scarves at the start line.
2) On go, the first runner takes one scarf, sprints forward, places it inside a hoop, and runs back.
3) The next runner can only leave the cone once tagged by the returning runner, placing another scarf strategically.
4) After all three scarves are played, subsequent runners sprint up to move one of their own scarves to an open hoop until one team aligns three in a row.
9 hula hoops, 6 scarves (3 per team), 2 cones

1) Stand at an appropriate distance facing a gym wall marked with a target area, holding a foam ball.
2) Point your non-throwing side toward the wall target and bring your throwing arm back into an uppercase L shape.
3) Step with the opposite foot, twist your torso, and throw the ball overhand at the target, catching the rebound.
